item.title: Training workshop on digital safety for women human rights defenders in Dhaka
item.description:
Digital safety is no longer an issue confined to technology experts; it has become an integral part of protecting and advancing human rights. Emphasising this connection, a training workshop titled “Digital Safety for Women Human Rights Defenders” was held Saturday at the YWCA Conference Room in Dhaka, reports a press release.

The workshop was organised by VOICE, a rights-based research and advocacy organisation, with the support of Association for Progressive Communications (APC). It brought together women journalists, women human rights defenders, and Indigenous rights activists to strengthen their understanding and capacity to address digital threats and promote safer online spaces.

Through practical, hands-on sessions, participants received training on multiple aspects of Digital hygiene and online privacy, fighting AI based online violence, threat modelling and digital safety planning, protecting social media identity and activism.

The digital safety strategies were presented by Musharrat Mahera and Priyata Tripura from VOICE. They remarked, “As women human rights defenders increasingly rely on digital platforms in their work, they face growing risks to their privacy, security, and sensitive information. Ensuring digital safety is therefore essential to protecting the information they handle, safeguarding their online presence, and enabling them to continue their human rights work without fear of digital threats or harassment.”

Digital safety and security specialist Tanvir Hasan Zoha said, “Protecting women human rights defenders in the digital space requires strong online privacy practices, responsible digital habits, and the knowledge and skills to identify and combat emerging forms of AI-driven violence and harassment.”

Digital safety professional Sadman Ahmed stated “Women human rights defenders need to understand their digital risks and develop proactive safety plans to protect themselves. Securing social media identities and online activism is essential to maintaining their digital presence, protecting their voices, and continuing their advocacy without fear.”

Ahmed Swapan Mahmud, executive director of VOICE, said, “Digital rights and freedom of expression are deeply interconnected, particularly for women human rights defenders who rely on digital platforms to raise their voices and advocate for justice. Ensuring a safe digital environment and strengthening digital literacy are essential to protecting their online identities, safeguarding their voices, and enabling them to exercise their freedom of expression without fear of harassment, threats, or intimidation.”

The workshop covered key topics through hands-on activities, including threat modeling for self-risk analysis, the use of artificial intelligence, strong passwords, two-factor authentication for critical social media accounts, VPNs, safe browsing with Tor Browser, encrypted communication, and data backup.

Participants also practiced identifying malicious links, safeguarding mobile devices and social media privacy, and protecting their digital security while reporting in the field; such as by avoiding public Wi-Fi and disabling geo-location tracking.

item.title: How birthday celebration becomes a major business success
item.description:
The birthday of Syed Manzur Elahi, the founding chairman of the domestic shoe company Apex Footwear, which dominates the shoe market, is on 26 September.

While he was alive, his established company, Apex Footwear, took the initiative to celebrate this day in a special way. As a result, the company began observing 26 September each year as ''Founder's Day".

Even after Syed Manzur Elahi's death, the company continues to celebrate the day with special arrangements. The celebration has now become a major ''opportunity'' for Apex's business, which the company claims as a ''major crown'' of success.

According to company sources, on ''Founder's Day", every 26 September, Apex offers special discounts on all types of products for customers.

Consequently, the company does several times more business on that day compared to regular days, significantly impacting the company's sales and profits. This year was no exception.

In the first quarter (July–September) of the current 2026-27 financial year, Apex Footwear conducted business worth Tk 5.51 billion. During the same period last year, it was Tk 4.83 billion. Comparatively, the company's business increased by Tk 680 million or more than 14 per cent in the first quarter of the current financial year compared to the same quarter of the previous financial year.

The significant influence of the 26 September ''Founder's Day'' sales is evident here. This year, Founder's Day was celebrated over two days, on 26 and 27 September, and the company did business of around Tk 700 million during these days, as stated by the company's Chief Marketing Officer, Md Raihan Kabir.

Speaking to multiple company officials revealed that the concept of ''Founder's Day'' was introduced in 2021 with the idea of celebrating Syed Manzur Elahi's birthday differently. The main objective of this celebration was to express special gratitude to customers on the founder's birthday—those who support the company by purchasing products throughout the year. To show appreciation to them, a 26 per cent discount is offered on all types of products on 26 September.

Company officials mentioned that on other days of the year, Apex Footwear sells shoes and other products worth Tk 30 million to Tk 40 million daily. On the day of the Founder's Day celebration, sales increase by 10-12 times. This year, the sales during the two-day Founder's Day celebration were close to the company's monthly sales. As a result, the company's sales and profits have been increasing in the July–September quarter for several years centering around Founder's Day sales.

Reviewing several years of financial reports from the July–September quarters, the authenticity of this information is evident. In the July–September quarter of the 2021-22 financial year, the company conducted business worth Tk 2.82 billion, earning a profit of approximately Tk 30 million.

In the same quarter of the 2022-23 financial year, they did business worth Tk 4.25 billion, making a profit of Tk 30 million. In the same quarter of the 2023-24 financial year, business was worth Tk 3.51 billion, with a profit of about Tk 20 million. In the 2024-25 financial year, they did business worth Tk 4.23 billion, earning a profit of approximately Tk 30 million.

In the July–September quarter of the 2025-26 financial year, the company conducted business worth Tk 4.84 billion, with a profit of about Tk 20 million. This year, for the first time, the company's sales or business exceeded Tk 5 billion in the July–September quarter, with a profit exceeding Tk 50 million. Compared to the same quarter of the previous year, Apex's profit more than doubled in the current year, with Founder's Day playing a significant role in this achievement.

Apex officials say that the celebration of the founder's birthday has now become a ''major crown'' of success for their business. The positive impact on the entire quarter's sales and profits is evident, with the celebration's sales continuing to achieve greater success as time passes.

When asked, Apex Footwear's Managing Director (MD) and Syed Manzur Elahi's son, Syed Nasim Manzur, told Prothom Alo, "Five years ago, we chose the founder's birthday to express gratitude and thanks to our consumers. The aim was to thank those consumers who support our business throughout the year. For this reason, we have been offering a 26 per cent discount on all types of products. Over a few years, this celebration has become a ''major crown'' of business success for us. We are deeply grateful to our customers for that."

It is known that ''Black Friday'' for retail sales in the United States has become known worldwide as a major shopping day or festival. Black Friday is celebrated the day after Thanksgiving, on the fourth Thursday of November every year.

On this day, all types of retail companies across the country offer various discounts for customers, with businesses seeing sales increase several times. Apex's Founder's Day has begun to take on a Black Friday-like festive sales significance for the company.

Omar Faruq, Apex's company secretary, said, "Over the past few years, Founder's Day has become a major celebration of business success for us. Many customers wait throughout the year for this celebration, and their interest positively impacts our business."

item.title: Health minister undergoes angiogram at Dhaka's Continental Hospital
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain underwent a cardiac angiogram at Continental Hospital in Dhaka on Saturday afternoon.
The procedure was performed by a team led by cardiologist Dr Moniruzzaman. The minister remains admitted to the hospital and is reported to be doing well.
Paban Chowdhury, public relations and senior information officer at the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune.
He said the minister had been planning to undergo the procedure for some time but had postponed it due to his busy schedule.
"Today's angiogram was part of his routine health check-up. He is currently admitted to the hospital and is doing well," Chowdhury said.

item.title: BGMEA: Scenario being created for announcing unreasonable wages
item.description:
Mahmud Hasan Khan, president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), has alleged that a pretext is being created to force an unreasonable wage announcement by destabilizing the readymade garment (RMG) industry.
He stated that chaos is still being instigated in factories despite the formation of the wage board, creating a situation designed to force an unreasonable wage hike under pressure.
He made these remarks while responding to journalists' questions at a joint press conference held by two garment owners' associations—BGMEA and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA)—at the BGMEA Complex in Uttara, Dhaka, on Saturday (November 14).
Also present at the press conference were BKMEA executive president Fazlee Shamim Ehsan, vice president Amal Poddar, and BGMEA vice presidents Rezwan Selim and Mizanur Rahman, among others.
Mahmud Hasan Khan said: "The wage board was formed on November 1. However, the chaotic situation began in the last week of October. Even if we consider what happened last month as reasonable, what is happening right now is by no means justified. The wage board has already been formed."
"Most importantly, the effective date for the increased wages was already announced at the board's very first meeting. Creating an anarchic situation even after that means setting the stage for an unreasonable wage declaration under pressure."
Khan reported that due to the ongoing unrest, 147 factories in Savar-Ashulia and Gazipur are unable to keep production running despite their best efforts.
On Saturday alone, 55 factories in these areas remained closed indefinitely under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, while 92 factories were forced to declare a holiday after failing to resume production.
He clarified that factories able to maintain regular operations are not permitted to shut down under Section 13(1).
However, regardless of the region, factories that cannot sustain production for even an hour despite their best efforts are legally entitled to close down due to a lack of security and a proper working environment.
In response to another question, Mahmud Hasan Khan said it is not possible for BGMEA to identify those behind the anarchy, noting that law enforcement agencies are working on it and have already brought the perpetrators under their surveillance network.
Earlier on Saturday morning, a joint view-exchange meeting was held with members of BGMEA and BKMEA at the BGMEA office auditorium, attended by over a thousand garment factory owners.
Conveying the opinions of the participating members, Mahmud Hasan Khan said that continuing discussions at the wage board becomes questionable if factory vandalism and road blockades persist simultaneously.
"However, as a responsible part of society, we will attend the third meeting of the wage board on Monday, November 16," he said, hoping that the situation will improve within the next 1-2 days.
If the situation does not improve, owners will sit together again to make a further decision, he added.

item.title: Gunmen fire on Mohammadpur pharmacy; Owner alleges Tk50 lakh extortion demand
item.description:
Two helmeted gunmen fired on Anurag Pharmacy on Babar Road in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, at 11:01pm on Friday, partially breaking its thick front glass in an attack that, according to one sales employee, narrowly missed his head, Prothom Alo reported.
Sales staff were handing medicine to a customer when a bullet struck the glass. Another shot was fired moments later. Panic spread among employees, customers and pedestrians.
Pharmacy sales employee Moin Uddin described the incident to Prothom Alo on Saturday afternoon in a frightened voice. He said: “The thick glass broke with a loud bang. Within moments, another bullet pierced the glass and passed beside my head. The bullet missed my head by a narrow margin. Otherwise, perhaps I would not have been alive today.”
Moin said the two helmet-wearing men were walking away quite normally after firing the shots. As several people were together at the pharmacy, they gathered the courage to chase the attackers. However, as soon as they came out and followed them, one of the men pulled out a large machete and threatened them. As a result, no one else dared to move forward. Later, the two attackers and another person got on a motorcycle and fled along the main road.
Jamil Islam, a sales employee at the pharmacy, told Prothom Alo that three people arrived on a motorcycle. One of them waited with the motorcycle some distance away, in front of Bangladesh Pharma. The other two went in front of the pharmacy and carried out the attack. One of them was carrying a large machete. After the attack, they got on the motorcycle and quickly left along the main road.
Footage from several CCTV cameras at nearby establishments captured the attack. Footage from one camera shows pedestrians moving normally along the footpath and road in front of the pharmacy. A white microbus was parked in front. Some distance away, a person was waiting with a motorcycle.
It was then 11:01pm. One of the two men, wearing a panjabi and a helmet, walked along the footpath. The other went towards the pharmacy along the main road. The shooting took place at this point. They then left the scene. Several people can be seen moving forward to chase them.
The distance between Anurag Pharmacy and the office of the deputy commissioner of police of the Tejgaon Division is approximately 500 metres. Moin Uddin alleged that immediately after the incident, they called the emergency service 999 and sought police assistance. However, nearly half an hour after receiving the call, a police team from the police station arrived at the scene and collected information from them.
Anurag Pharmacy is located beside the main road towards Shyamoli, opposite the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases. A visit to the location on Saturday afternoon found that beside the pharmacy, there are two consecutive restaurants and a super shop under the same establishment’s name. The glass at the front of the pharmacy had shattered and was scattered around after the shooting. However, customers were still visiting the premises.
An official involved in the police investigation told Prothom Alo that the establishment’s owner, Syed Hasan Nur Islam (Raston), is a former councillor of Ward 32 of Dhaka South City Corporation. He was Awami League-backed and is an accused in several cases filed after the mass uprising on August 5, 2024. He is currently absconding. The official said that although the owner was absconding, his businesses were still operating, and his political rivals from his own party or another group might be trying to take advantage of the situation surrounding the operation of his businesses. However, the investigation is considering several possible reasons.
Nur Islam, who is listed as an absconding accused in police records, told Prothom Alo over the mobile phone on Saturday evening that he is a businessman and a former councillor of the area, with no personal enmity or dispute with anyone. “I have never engaged in the politics of attacks and cases. I have a good reputation in the area,” he said. He listed the businesses in the building as Anurag Pharma, Anurag Restaurant, a Chinese restaurant, a super shop and a telecom business.
He alleged that on November 6, he received a phone call from a local mobile number demanding Tk50 lakh in extortion money. The caller used the names “Killer Badal” and “Killer Pappu”. He was threatened that if he did not pay, shots would be fired at his establishment Anurag, and everything would be vandalised and set on fire. He said he refused, ended the call and blocked the number, which was later handed over to law enforcement agencies. He claimed the attack was carried out because he had refused to pay.
He said that on November 5, a day before the extortion demand, two cocktails were exploded in front of the establishment, and several pedestrians were injured. After the demand on November 6, another cocktail attack took place on November 7. Then, on November 13, two shots were fired at the establishment, and the glass at the front of the pharmacy broke. No one was injured or killed. He said a written complaint about the shooting was submitted to the police station on Saturday.
Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) of the Tejgaon Division Md Juel Rana told Prothom Alo on Saturday evening that the incident was under investigation. CCTV footage was being analysed and other information and evidence were being examined to uncover the actual mystery of the incident and identify those involved and bring them under the law.

item.title: 37 teenagers jailed over Joy Bangla slogans in Munshiganj
item.description:
A court has ordered 37 teenagers arrested for chanting “Joy Bangla” slogans aboard a trawler in the Dhaleshwari River near Munshiganj town to be sent to jail.
Police produced them before two separate courts on Saturday afternoon. Following separate hearings, judges of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court and the Children’s Court ordered their detention in jail.
Munshiganj Court Police Inspector Md Kamrul Islam Mia confirmed the matter.
He said the teenagers were produced before the two courts separately and that both judges ordered them sent to jail after hearing their cases.
Earlier, on Friday afternoon, a group of teenagers was seen chanting “Joy Bangla” slogans aboard a vessel in the Dhaleshwari River near the Mollar Char area of Munshiganj town.
Police initially detained seven to eight teenagers from a vessel. Later, local leaders and activists of the Jubo Dal and Chhatra Dal detained several others and handed them over to police.
Munshiganj Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Taslim Uddin said police had taken positions along the riverbank after receiving information that activists of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League had gathered aboard vessels in the Dhaleshwari River to plan subversive activities.
Police subsequently detained several suspected individuals who arrived together on a trawler. Later, local Chhatra Dal and Jubo Dal activists detained several more teenagers from an anchored cargo vessel and handed them over to police.
The 37 teenagers were sent to court on Saturday under Section 151 of the Code of Criminal Procedure over allegations of gathering to plan subversive activities, the OC said. The court later ordered them sent to jail.

item.title: Bangladesh, Türkiye discuss strengthening cooperation in trade, renewable energy
item.description:
Bangladesh and Türkiye have discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, technology transfer, renewable energy, waste management and people-to-people engagement.
The discussion took place when Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Türkiye, Ambassador A Berris Ekinci, met State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam at the Bangladesh Pavilion on Friday on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.
During the meeting, the two sides discussed various issues of mutual interest and stressed the need to enhance cooperation in different areas.
They also underscored the importance of working together to address environmental challenges affecting both countries and the wider international community.
Shama Obaed congratulated the Turkish deputy minister on the successful organisation of COP31 and thanked the Turkish government for its warm hospitality towards the delegates.
She also appreciated the Zero Waste initiative under the patronage of the First Lady of Türkiye, noting its alignment with Bangladesh's own 3R (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) strategy.
Both sides highlighted the importance of sharing experiences and best practices in sustainable waste management.
The state minister sought Türkiye's cooperation in promoting jute and jute-based products as eco-friendly and biodegradable alternatives to plastic.
She said Bangladesh's jute sector has significant potential to contribute to global efforts to reduce plastic pollution and promote environmentally responsible consumption.
Shama Obaed also invited the Turkish deputy minister to visit Bangladesh at a mutually convenient time.
The state minister presented jute-made handicrafts to the deputy minister as a souvenir.

item.title: Bomb-like object found on Jamalpur railway overpass, panic spreads
item.description:
Police and Fire Service personnel rushed to the scene and cordoned off the area following reports of the suspicious object.
According to police and local sources, several pedestrians spotted the object while crossing the overpass and alerted police, suspecting it to be a bomb because of the wires attached to both ends.
Jamalpur Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Nazmus Sakib said police and Fire Service personnel were at the scene to secure the area.
"Whether the object is actually a bomb has yet to be confirmed. Efforts are underway to recover it," he said.

item.title: Fugitive son arrested in Gopalganj over father's murder in Narail
item.description:
A youth accused of killing his father in Narail's Lohagara upazila has been arrested in Gopalganj.
The arrestee, Khairul Sheikh, 25, is the son of the victim, Afsar Sheikh and a resident of Boyra area in Lohagara of the district.
Lt Col Nistar Ahmed, commander of SRB-6, said an operational team from the Bhatia Para Camp arrested Khairul in front of the Upazila Muktijoddha Complex in Gopalganj Sadar around 4:15pm on Saturday, acting on a tip-off.
Khairul is the prime accused in the murder case. He was later handed over to Lohagara Police Station in Narail for further legal action.
According to the case statement, Khairul had been involved in a family dispute with his father over various domestic issues.
On November 5, around 12:30pm, he allegedly attacked his father with a sharp boti (traditional cutting knife), striking him on the head and leaving him seriously injured.
As Afsar fell to the ground, Khairul allegedly struck him again in the chest with the same weapon, causing severe injuries that exposed his lungs.
The victim's elder son later filed a murder case with Lohagara Police Station against Khairul and two others.

item.title: Shahzad's late strike breaks Bangladesh heart, sends Pakistan into SAFF final
item.description:
Bangladesh's hopes of reaching the SAFF Championship final were dashed as Pakistan secured a historic 1-0 victory in the exciting second semifinal at the National Stadium on Saturday, booking their place in the title decider for the first time.
Abdul Samad Shahzad struck the decisive goal late in the match to send Pakistan into the final, where they will face arch-rivals India on November 17 at the same venue.
India earlier booked their place in the final for the 10th time, defeating Bhutan 2-1 in the day's first semifinal.
The defeat ended Bangladesh's hopes of returning to the SAFF final, having last reached the title decider in 2005.
Bangladesh enjoyed the better of the opening half, dominating possession and creating several scoring opportunities, but poor finishing let them down.
They threatened as early as the seventh minute when Syed Quazem Kirmanee, set up by Rakib Hossain, unleashed a left-footed effort from outside the box, only for Pakistan goalkeeper Yousuf to make a comfortable save.
Bangladesh came close again in the 22nd minute. Farhaan Ali Wahid delivered a corner from the right, and Rakib attempted a shot from inside the box, but the Pakistani goalkeeper intervened to keep the hosts at bay.
Pakistan, meanwhile, nearly took the lead in the 32nd minute when Abdullah controlled a cross from the middle of the pitch and fired a shot that beat the goalkeeper but struck the post before going out for a corner.
Bangladesh finished the first half with 59 percent possession, compared to Pakistan's 41 percent. Hamza Choudhury was influential in midfield, dictating the play, creating opportunities in attack and tracking back to support the defence. Pakistan largely relied on counter-attacks.
After the break, Pakistan looked more organised and gradually increased the pressure on the Bangladesh defence as both teams searched for the breakthrough.
Pakistan came close in the 75th minute when Adil Bani unleashed a powerful free-kick, but Bangladesh goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon produced an excellent diving save to his left, punching the ball away. Srabon was called into action again six minutes later when substitute Najeeb Ullah beat a defender and fired from the edge of the box. The Bangladesh custodian dived to his right to punch the ball clear.
However, Pakistan finally broke the deadlock in the 86th minute. Receiving a close pass, Shahzad fired a left-footed angled shot beyond Srabon's reach to seal the victory and send Pakistan into their maiden SAFF Championship final.
Bangladesh tried their best to stage a fight back creating some chances but could not find the net in the remaining proceeding
Earlier, Bangladesh made two changes to their starting XI, with Rahmat Mia replacing the injured Saad Uddin and Shuki Itofusa coming in for Mohammad Ibrahim.
Mehedi Hasan Srabon started in goal, with Zayyan Ahmed, Tariq Raihan Kazi and Zidane Yousuf forming the defensive line. Topu Barman and Bishwanath Ghosh were left out of the starting XI.
Hamza Choudhury, Shamit Shome and Shah Quazem Kirmanee anchored the midfield, while Rakib Hossain, Farhaan Ali Wahid and Shuki Itofusa led the attack.
Head coach Thomas Dooley fielded eight expatriate players in the starting XI. Jamal Bhuyan, who featured in Bangladesh's previous match against Sri Lanka, was left out.

item.title: PM orders inclusion of retired officials in Dhaka cleanliness drives
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has directed authorities to involve retired government officials and senior citizens in neighbourhood-level cleanliness campaigns to help build a “Clean Dhaka, Green Dhaka”.
The directive came at a review meeting on the capital’s cleanliness activities at the Prime Minister’s Office on Saturday, State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam said at a briefing.
Around 39,000 retired government employees live in Dhaka. They will serve as advisers or take up responsibilities in neighbourhood committees, working alongside young volunteers and government officials.
The campaign will focus on dengue prevention, proper waste disposal, keeping footpaths clear, improving drainage and ensuring household waste reaches secondary transfer stations (STSs).
Committees formed around the 20 regional offices of Dhaka’s two city corporations have so far inspected 248 educational institutions, 129 hospitals and clinics, 112 government residential areas, 152 markets and shopping complexes, and 188 roads, parks and public spaces. They have also visited 130 other sites, including bus terminals and railway stations.
The prime minister has directed authorities to establish more STSs, including exploring environmentally friendly underground facilities, as existing capacity is inadequate for the capital.
The meeting also decided to consider making icddr,b’s medical waste management system mandatory for hospitals and clinics. Government residential accommodation could be cancelled if occupants fail to manage waste properly and maintain hygienic conditions, Shahe Alam said.
To address a shortage of cleaning workers, the government has approved the recruitment of 2,000 workers for Dhaka South City Corporation and 1,500 for Dhaka North City Corporation.
The committees will continue their work, with the prime minister scheduled to review progress again in a month.

item.title: 13 garment factories shut indefinitely in Gazipur amid workers’ unrest
item.description:
Thirteen garment factories in Gazipur have been declared closed indefinitely due to workers’ unrest. Five other factories have also announced a holiday for today, Sunday. Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, confirmed the closure to Prothom Alo.

According to industrial police and local sources, workers at a garment factory in the Jarun area of Konabari in Gazipur city, began protesting at around 8:30 am today. After receiving the news, police fired tear gas and sound grenades to disperse them.

RMG owners announce closure from tomorrow if workers do not report for work

Meanwhile, after several factories in the Mouchak area of Kaliakair announced a holiday at around 9:00 am, garment workers held a protest march and gathered in front of the Hydro Oxide Limited garment factory.

They tried to block the Dhaka–Tangail Highway. Members of law enforcement agencies arrived and moved the workers away. As a result, no further disorder occurred in the area.

Gazipur Industrial Police superintendent told Prothom Alo that workers had tried to gather at separate locations in the morning but were unable to do so because of law enforcement activities. Members of the forces have been deployed at every key point in the industrial areas.

Several thousand workers are employed at Far East Knitting and Dyeing Industries in the East Chandra area of Kaliakair upazila. The factory has been declared closed indefinitely from today.

In a notice issued today, the factory authorities said the decision had been taken following vandalism at the factory and attacks on its officials and employees amid ongoing workers’ unrest over demands for a minimum wage.

The notice also stated that, despite clear statements from the government and the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) on the approval, publication and implementation of the minimum wage, unrest among outside workers demanding the announcement of the wage had turned destructive.

Workers' side seeks Tk 32,000 minimum wage in RMG sector

Agitated individuals entered the factory and vandalised it, causing extensive damage. Workers and officials were left bloodied and injured. In view of the situation, all factory operations have been suspended under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006, the notice added.

Besides Far East, at least 13 factories have been declared closed indefinitely. They include Ecotex Limited, Ahsan Composite and Apex Holding Limited in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area, and Moazzuddin Textile Limited in Mouchak area.

item.title: Awami League seeks attention by announcing Sheikh Hasina’s return
item.description:
The Awami League, whose activities are banned, is seeking to attract attention both at home and internationally by announcing that Sheikh Hasina will return to Bangladesh in December.

To this end, the party and the banned student organisation Chhatra League are announcing various programmes online, including ‘strikes’ and ‘lockdowns’. However, even Awami League leaders have no clear idea how the announcement of Sheikh Hasina’s return to the country will be implemented.

Some Awami League leaders who are in hiding say that, under the current circumstances Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh is almost impossible without a diplomatic understanding between the governments of Bangladesh and India.

Cooperation from the international community would also be needed to create such circumstances. However, there are still no signs of any understanding between the two governments over Sheikh Hasina, they say.

Some Awami League leaders fear that if Sheikh Hasina fails to return after making the announcement, public confidence in her or the Awami League could decline. Meanwhile, the announced programmes are putting party leaders and activists in the country at risk of being arrested again.

Sheikh Hasina, the former prime minister who was ousted in the July mass uprising and is the president of the Awami League, has announced that she will return to Bangladesh from India in December.

Sheikh Hasina will return through legal process, what India will do is up to them: Law Minister

The announcement has sparked widespread discussion about whether Hasina, who has been sentenced to death, will actually return and, if she does, what process she will follow to come back to the country.

The government’s position on the matter is clear: Sheikh Hasina is a fugitive who has been sentenced to death. If she is to return to Bangladesh, it must be under the Bangladesh-India extradition treaty. Bangladesh has also formally requested India to extradite her.

With December approaching, the Awami League, whose activities are banned, and the banned Chhatra League are announcing various programmes online. As part of these, they called a strike for 10 November.

Although the strike was not carried out, incidents of sabotage, including sporadic crude bomb explosions and vehicles being set on fire, have taken place in Dhaka and various other parts of the country on 10 November and in the days before and after.

Many leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations have expressed support for these activities online. Some have even claimed responsibility for them.

Law enforcement agencies are also blaming leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations for these acts of sabotage. Operations to arrest them have been stepped up. Law enforcement agencies have also claimed to have caught people red-handed while they were involved in crude bomb explosions in Dhaka.

Sheikh Hasina faces 673 cases, including 457 on murder charges

Meanwhile, on 13 November, the Awami League announced a five-day programme on its Facebook page to mark the anniversary of the verdict sentencing Sheikh Hasina to death.

Yesterday, Saturday, the programme included distributing leaflets, writing on walls, conducting publicity campaigns and reaching out to people. However, no reports of such activities have emerged. Further programmes include processions, submitting memorandums and wearing black badges. A ‘lockdown’ has been announced for 19 November.

Most of the Awami League’s senior leaders are in India, particularly in Kolkata. Several sources within the party said that many leaders based in countries including the United States and various European nations had also travelled to India recently. Some of them are still there.

Sources close to these leaders said they had no clear idea of how the announcement that Sheikh Hasina would return to Bangladesh in December was to be implemented.

Discussion surrounding announcement of return

Reuters reported on 9 November that Sheikh Hasina had written to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi seeking a passport and national identity card. The application was sent in an email by Matrix Chambers, a London-based law firm in the United Kingdom (UK).

However, diplomatic sources in Dhaka and New Delhi said the email sent by the law firm did not include any document or proof relating to Sheikh Hasina’s ‘authorisation’.

Jaiswal declines to comment on reports that Delhi wants Bangladesh to send military aircraft to bring Hasina back

Meanwhile, BBC Bangla published a report last Friday on Sheikh Hasina’s announcement that she would return to Bangladesh. The report gave the impression that she did not make the announcement without India’s consent.

The BBC Bangla report also mentioned two conditions set by India. First, Sheikh Hasina travelled to India on a Bangladeshi military aircraft. If she is to be brought back, the Bangladesh Army must take responsibility for doing so. Her return could be by land or air.

Second, Bangladesh would have to guarantee that Sheikh Hasina would have the opportunity to appeal against her death sentence and that the trial over the July mass killings would be held afresh.

However, Bangladeshi diplomatic sources do not yet see any basis for such conditions being imposed.

Government stresses extradition treaty

Saturday, journalists asked Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman about the legal process concerning Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh, referring to the BBC report. In response, the law minister said, “Sheikh Hasina will come to Bangladesh through legal means. We have completed all the necessary legal procedures on our part. What they (India) will do is their own matter.”

Referring to the International Crimes Tribunal Act, the law minister said that anyone accused or convicted of crimes against humanity could not claim fundamental rights.

If Sheikh Hasina wants to return, govt will act under extradition treaty

Asked whether the Indian government had held discussions with Bangladesh about sending Sheikh Hasina to a third country the law minister said, “They would be able to say anything about that.”

After reports emerged that Sheikh Hasina had applied for a new passport and national identity card (NID) to return to the country, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir described the matter as “utterly ridiculous” on 9 November.

He said that Bangladesh did not issue passports to terrorists. Instead, it wanted to bring them back to the country under the extradition treaty and carry out their sentences.

Humaiun Kobir also said, “She has fled, and there is no scope for staging a drama about returning to the country with a new passport. If she genuinely wants to return, there is a specific legal process for that. Bangladesh and India have an extradition treaty.”

“Let her ask the Indian government to hand her over to Bangladesh under that treaty. She can come here, surrender to the court and serve her sentence,” he added.

Appeal deadline has passed

On 17 November last year, the International Crimes Tribunal sentenced Sheikh Hasina to death in a case involving crimes against humanity committed during the July mass uprising. The full verdict in the case was published on 13 January.

Appeals must be filed within 30 days, whether by Sheikh Hasina or Abul Kalam Azad

The International Crimes Tribunal Act provides for a 30-day period to appeal. However, Sheikh Hasina did not file an appeal within the stipulated time.

Sources at the tribunal said that, as the appeal period had expired, she no longer had the opportunity to appeal. In addition to the death sentence, the tribunal also ordered the confiscation of Sheikh Hasina’s property in Bangladesh in favour of the state.

Six other cases against Sheikh Hasina are pending trial at the tribunal. In addition, a total of 673 cases have been filed against her, including 457 over allegations of murder in different parts of the country.

Against this backdrop, questions have also been raised within the Awami League about the purpose of the party’s programmes and activities surrounding the announcement of Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh.

A central Awami League leader in hiding, speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, said that holding programmes in this way would not secure the demands or make Sheikh Hasina’s return to the country possible. Everything suggested that the main aim of these programmes was to attract attention at home and internationally, the leader said.

How much attention they would receive remained to be seen. However, the programmes would anger the government and increase the risks facing party leaders and activists in Bangladesh, the leader added.

item.title: Police super arrested in Chattogram sedition case over alleged links to Awami League
item.description:

Gazipur garment workers return to work; security tightened
item.description:
Security has been tightened across Gazipur's industrial belt following recent workers' unrest over demands for a higher minimum wage, with 25 platoons of law enforcement personnel deployed under the supervision of 25 executive magistrates.
Workers began returning to their duties at various garment factories on Sunday morning. No fresh incidents of protests or road blockades had been reported in the industrial areas as of 8:30am. However, authorities have declared a holiday at six garment factories as a precautionary measure.
Arif Hossain, assistant commissioner of the Media and Research Cell at the Gazipur Deputy Commissioner's Office, confirmed the information on Sunday morning.
He said 13 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), five platoons of Ansar and eight platoons of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) had been deployed to maintain law and order. The forces are operating under the supervision of 25 executive magistrates.
Arif added that law enforcement agencies remained on high alert to prevent damage to public and private property or disruption to public life. BGB personnel had already begun operations, while other units remained on standby.
Earlier, garment workers in different parts of Gazipur staged protests and blocked the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, demanding an increase in the minimum wage.
During the unrest, incidents of arson were reported at police outposts, police vehicles and factory warehouses. Several clashes also broke out between protesters and law enforcement personnel, leaving workers and members of the security forces injured. Several people were detained in connection with the incidents.
Following the unrest, a number of garment factories in Gazipur announced holidays.
Meanwhile, a worker named Taufiq died after being beaten while recording the protests on his mobile phone.

item.title: Chittagong RRF SP arrested over alleged Awami League links, information leak
item.description:
Jahangir Alam, superintendent of police (SP) of the Chittagong Range Reserve Force (RRF), has been arrested in a sedition case over allegations of maintaining contact with the now-banned Awami League and leaking sensitive police information.
His personal and official mobile phones had been seized, and he was placed under surveillance before his arrest.
Following approval from the Ministry of Home Affairs, RRF Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Abul Kashem Chowdhury filed a case against him at Panchlaish police station around 10:30pm on Saturday. Later that night, a joint team of the Special Response Unit (SRU), Counter-Terrorism Unit and Panchlaish police arrested him at the Officers' Mess.
Chittagong Metropolitan Police (CMP) Commissioner Hasan Shawkat Ali confirmed the arrest, saying the Ministry of Home Affairs had approved the action on Friday.
According to police sources, Chittagong Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Abdul Kuddus Chowdhury questioned Jahangir last Tuesday after preliminary evidence of the alleged incident emerged.
His personal and official mobile phones were seized the same day and sent to the police Special Branch (SB) headquarters in Dhaka for forensic examination.
Meanwhile, an internal departmental investigation is underway, led by Shafijul Islam, additional DIG (Operations) of the Chittagong Range.
Sources at the Chittagong Range office said Jahangir had been summoned over allegations that he shared internal and sensitive police information with Awami League leaders and activists, despite the party's activities being currently prohibited.
Citing the first information report (FIR), a CMP official told the media that a message allegedly sent from Jahangir's mobile phone referred to people taking to the streets in December, describing them as swarming "like bees".
The message also reportedly referred to his participation in the 1996 movement demanding a caretaker government and expressed support for the ideals of Bangabandhu. It further included a statement about "rescuing" Bangladesh.
However, the identity of the message's recipient has not been established.
Sources said the investigation could be assigned to a specialised police unit, such as the SRU or the Counter-Terrorism Unit.

item.title: What empty malls can teach us about getting richer
item.description:
How new technology makes us all richer can be a little difficult to work through. We can all see -- because it's obvious -- how rich the entrepreneurs who own the new technology get.
Jeff Bezos, for example, has a second yacht to carry his helicopter while following his first yacht. Which is, you know, pretty rich. Mark Zuckerberg has half a Hawaiian island and Ellison, of Oracle, has most of another -- both also have large yachts.
But what do we get out of this arrangement? One of the reasons populist politicians gain so much attraction from voters is that tracking that down can be difficult. There are answers. Zuckerberg's fortune comes from, in part, us getting free telephone calls on WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger. OK, free phone calls may or may not be of huge value to us individually but there are 4 billion of us -- half the entire world -- who get them which does add up.
The very existence of Amazon has cut 0.1 to 0.2% off the US inflation rate for two decades now. Just that price competition from it has lowered all prices for everyone by 2-4% on everything they buy. That's worth one yacht, maybe two.
We can also look at this in more detail in Bangladesh. Owners of shopping malls in Dhaka are selling up. Because they cannot make money any more and the reason is : “The rise of online retail,” “shop online,” the “expansion of e-commerce,” and so on.
We see this in my native Britain as well. The Office for National Statistics records that online sales are 28% of total retail sales today -- up from 3% in 2006. As a result, we simply require fewer shops and it's true that retail landlords are suffering. At least one of the large companies -- Intu -- went bust some years back as a result.
This doesn't mean that no one ever wants to go to the shops and everyone wants to only buy online. There really are those who enjoy going shopping just for the joy of going shopping.
What we're therefore seeing in some other countries is a division in the shopping experience. Yes, we still have little local shops where we can get little supplies of necessities -- a gallon of milk, a loaf of bread. We also have the big shopping experiences of places where it's possible to go and have a day out having that active fun of shopping.
The places feeling the financial pressure are those that used to provide the shopping that had to be done and that few find that fun. That's now better -- or preferentially -- done by point, click, and the delivery van.
These things are all true but we do tend to not put as much emphasis on these benefits to us -- even as they clearly are benefits because this is why we do things -- as we do upon the problems of those going bust because we've changed our ways.
We also tend not to feel a 1 or 2% change in price levels, or any other gradual change, over years. Even as they are how we get richer over time. One and two percent really does add up over decades.
Then along comes an economist and points out that this isn't, not really, how we all get richer. The real point is this: “As a result, the owners decided to sell off the property. Discussions are currently underway with several entities, including hospitals, corporate firms, and banks.”
Dhaka has a limited amount of land. As the most densely populated city on the planet, it has a very limited amount of land. So, if we stop using land for one purpose, then we get empty land that can then be used for another.
We're made richer by whatever value we put upon having a hospital, more jobs and employment from corporations, or even a bank -- hopefully one that doesn't lose all the money.
And that is how economists say we get richer. This new way of doing things, this new technology, uses fewer resources -- less land here, but it can be less labour, less energy, etc -- and this means we've now newly freed up resources to go and produce something else that we want.
We are richer by whatever value we put on this new thing that it is now possible to produce for our enjoyment. OK, hospitals aren't really about enjoyment other than in the leaving of them alive. But you get the point.
Economists are indeed strange people, but they really do say that we get richer when we stop using resources. Because when we don't use something in limited supply to do this thing, here, that then frees up the supply of that thing to be used to do something else. We are richer by the value we place on that new thing being done.
Tim Worstall is a senior fellow at the Adam Smith Institute in London.

item.title: The growing threat of fake photocards
item.description:
A teenager’s body hangs from the Shaheed Minar in Manikganj. Beside it sits the portrait of an SSC examinee named Shihab, under a headline styled like Samakal’s: He scored a golden GPA-5 two days after his death. The photocard adds one more detail. It says the boy belonged to the Chhatra League.
FactWatch investigated this photocard in August 2026 and rated it false. Two different boys who shared a name had been merged into one story. Samakal’s real report was about a different Shihab. A dead child, a party label, and a trusted masthead: That mix is built to make people angry before they think.
Not a fluke, but a format
Between September 2025 and February 2026, fact-checkers debunked 690 distinct fake photocards. Nearly half of them were political misinformation.
Five simple elements are being used:
Prof Sumon Rahman, Head of the Media Studies and Journalism Department, ULAB, says the photocards are easy to produce and seem to carry a newsroom’s endorsement.
FactWatch’s 2021 review already found visuals and videos were the favourite carriers of falsehood. Rumor Scanner logged 105 fake photocards in 2023, then 324 cases in just nine months of 2024.
FactWatch spent the 10 weeks around Bangladesh’s 13th parliamentary election tracking exactly this. Between December 11, 2025 and February 17, 2026, its researchers logged and verified 94 distinct disinformation cases tied to the vote.
The breakdown is the interesting part: AI-generated content 16%, doctored excerpts 6%, and fake media photocards, the branded ones mimicking a specific outlet’s logo and layout, at 21%.
Made for big moments
Photocards follow the news cycle. Volumes spiked right after each major political event. After Osman Hadi was shot in December 2025, photocards about laundered money and invented quotes multiplied. When Tarique Rahman returned on December 25, others claimed patients were dying in ambulances.
The pattern predates that vote. During talk of Dr Yunus resigning in May 2025, 56% of that episode’s misinformation used fake photocards. Even a local union parishad race in Pirojpur drew fake photocards. Amar Desh’s design was copied the most, followed by Kaler Kantho, Jamuna Television, RTV, and Kalbela.
What is trending now
Artificial intelligence is the newest layer. FactWatch debunked an August 2026 card attributed to the power minister, and its detection tools suggested it was AI-generated. One study found 28% of AI cases were AI-edited photocards carrying false quotes.
Two other trends are more concerning. Photocards have turned sexual: Researchers counted 34 degrading cases, including a fake gang-rape claim about Dr Mahmuda Mitu . They stoke communal fear, such as invented threats to Hindu households over which symbol they vote for.
Who makes them, and why
Dismislab traced photocards to partisan pages across the spectrum. Roughly 62% attacked parties, 16% targeted individuals, and 12.5% puffed up popularity. A polls-day review found pro-Jamaat networks especially active, while Rumour Scanner says Indian accounts and local pages both feed wider campaigns against Bangladesh.
Spoof pages do the heavy lifting. FactWatch found that fake Amar Desh photocards spread from a look-alike page with about 14,000 followers, not the newspaper’s official one.
During the election period, multiple media outlets -- including Kaler Kantho, DBC News, Jamuna TV, Channel24, Jugantor, Amar Desh, BBC Bangla, and Prothom Alo -- had their identities spoofed, creating a network too expansive for any individual newsroom to track.
The readers who pay
A photocard is built for a thumb and a hurry, which suits newcomers. One national survey found 53% of adults are online, half for under five years, and about 40% of users are unfamiliar with search engines.
Unicef’s study found news literacy very low among people without high-school education. One analyst calls the problem a threat to a digitally illiterate population.
In an interview study of 29 Bangladeshi users, lower-education participants leaned on people. A driver said that if his boss shares something, he assumes it is credible. A housewife re-shares her sister’s posts because the sister is a government official. A retired man asks his granddaughter before he shares.
Now picture a photocard landing in that chain. It carries a familiar logo, so the outlet vouches for it. It comes from a cousin or a neighbour, so the family vouches for it. Two layers of borrowed trust arrive before anyone has read a word.
A Bangladesh misinformation primer notes that in some rural areas, people know Facebook but not the wider internet. Messaging apps like Imo, popular among migrant workers, carry rumours without any editor in the loop. A photocard that would take a scroll to debunk online can travel through a bazaar as paper. Nobody in that crowd opens a fact-checker’s page.
It also assumes the outlet’s page is easy to find. Outlets already post clarification notices, but they reach only the page followers.
When fake photocards multiply, the honest ones lose value. Readers learn that a logo proves nothing, and then they start to suspect real reporting too. Amar Desh’s editor warned that people begin to think the paper publishes fake news.
There is a cruel twist. A person caught out by one fake photocard often decides all photocards are fake. Disbelief becomes as useful to manipulators as belief. He may think the media is dying too. I worry now that a real piece of news can just be waved away as “just a photocard.”
Zulker Naeen is a research coordinator, Center for Critical and Qualitative Studies, and adjunct faculty, Department of Media Studies and Journalism, University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh.

item.title: Korail slum fire leaves one dead
item.description:
A young man was killed, and at least 7-8 shanties and a shop were gutted in a fire at the T&T Colony of the capital's Korail slum early Sunday.
The deceased was identified as Shahriar Rahman Shuvro, 19, son of Md Monir Hossain. Hailing from Shirjugh village in Jhalakathi Sadar upazila, he was a tenant of one Islam at Satellite Gate in T&T Colony.
Duty officer at the Fire Service and Civil Defence control room Rakibul Hasan said they received information about the fire at 4:53am and immediately dispatched three units to the spot.
The fire was brought under control around 6am, he said, adding that one person was killed in the incident.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage were not immediately known.

Attempt made to harass Nahid Islam at Cambridge University campus
item.description:
A group of activists and supporters of the Awami League, whose activities are banned in Bangladesh, attempted to harass Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizen Party (NCP), on the campus of the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom.

However, they failed to do so due to the intervention of NCP activists in the UK.

Nahid Islam, chief whip of the opposition in parliament and one of the key figures behind the July mass uprising that toppled the Awami League government, is currently visiting the UK on a week-long trip.

He attended an exchange of views organised by the Cambridge University Bangla Society at the main lecture theatre of the Old Divinity School at St John's College, University of Cambridge, on Saturday evening (local time).

After the event, as Nahid was getting into a car to leave the venue, he came face to face with a group of Awami League supporters who had gathered there beforehand.

Mohammad MA Himel, immediate past member secretary of the NCP UK Alliance, was present at the scene.

Around midnight Bangladesh time, he posted a video of the incident on his verified Facebook account. The video shows several expatriate Bangladeshis supporting the NCP helping Nahid into a car.

Meanwhile, another group of NCP supporters were engaged in a heated exchange with several Awami League supporters near the front of the vehicle. The car carrying Nahid left the scene amid the commotion.

In the caption accompanying the video, Himel wrote: “This is how we exit Nahid Islam from the Cambridge University seminar. Awami League couldn't even touch us!”

In another video posted by Himel, NCP supporters can be seen chanting slogans against the Awami League.

Its caption read: “NCP gives a crushing response to Awami League's goons in Cambridge.”

Asked about the incident, Ehteshamul Haque, convener of the preparation committee for Nahid Islam's UK visit, told Prothom Alo today that the Awami League had repeatedly attempted to harass NCP leaders in the UK.

“They tried to do the same last night but failed. Nahid Islam successfully completed his programme at Cambridge University and left the venue. However, Awami League activists shouted slogans outside,” he said.

''They failed to gain any ground''

The attempt to harass Nahid Islam in the UK has sparked anger among NCP leaders and activists. They allege that the same individual organised both the attempt to harass Nahid and an earlier incident involving NCP leader Hasnat Abdullah in the UK. They claim the person has been identified.

Sarwar Tushar, a member of the NCP Political Council, the party's highest policymaking body, and its joint convener, told Prothom Alo that Awami League supporters gathered outside the venue of Nahid Islam's programme at Cambridge University and chanted various slogans.

“But they failed to gain any ground because many NCP supporters were present there. In fact, they try to harass everyone associated with the July uprising. Since Nahid Islam was one of the leading faces of the uprising, it is natural that they harbour resentment towards him,” he said.

“But they are no longer getting much response. Apart from 10 to 15 extremists, nobody is turning up. This is a sign that they are losing strength and becoming demoralised,” he added.

Identifying a person currently residing in the UK and supporting the Awami League as the organiser of these incidents, Sarwar Tushar said the individual had already been identified.

“The Bangladesh government can take legal action against him or seek his deportation if it wishes,” he said.

Runa Khan accepts the 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award in Manila
item.description:
Runa Khan, founder of Friendship, received the 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award at a ceremony at the Metropolitan Theatre (MET Theatre) in Manila on Sunday, 15 November. The ceremony was followed by a gala dinner honouring this year’s laureates.

Earlier, on 11 November, Khan delivered a lecture reflecting on her journey and the experiences that shaped her work as a humanitarian and social innovator. Francisco Magsaysay, grandson of former Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay, formally presented the 68th Ramon Magsaysay Award 2026 to Friendship Founder Runa Khan.

Widely regarded as Asia’s premier recognition for public service and transformative leadership, and often described as the “Nobel Prize of Asia”, the Ramon Magsaysay Award was established in memory of former Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay. First presented in 1958, it recognised individuals and organisations whose work demonstrated courage, integrity, and service to the region. By 2026, it had honoured 359 individuals and organisations across 24 countries and territories in Asia. Khan became the 14th Bangladeshi recipient.

Recognition of a vision for inclusive development

In electing Runa Khan to receive the 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award, the board of trustees recognises her profound empathy for the poorest of the poor in her country, and her courage, vision, and tenacity in building and leading Friendship to accomplish her mission. In her hands, privilege became not an entitlement, but a responsibility; not a family legacy to protect, but a gift to be shared so that others, too, might have the chance to live with hope, opportunity, and dignity.

Runa Khan’s journey began in 1997, when she encountered the realities of life on Bangladesh’s remote chars — shifting river islands exposed to erosion, flooding, and displacement, where communities often lacked reliable access to healthcare, education, and other essential services. She founded Friendship in 2002, beginning with a pioneering floating hospital that brought healthcare to people beyond the reach of conventional services.

Over more than two decades, Friendship grew into an integrated social purpose organisation working across healthcare, education, climate adaptation, sustainable economic development, inclusive citizenship, and cultural preservation. Together, they serve four commitments—saving lives, poverty alleviation, climate adaptation and empowerment, which collectively address all 17 Sustainable Development Goals though integrated, holistic development solutions. The organisation reaches approximately 7.5 million people each year, developing locally led solutions that connect essential services with long-term resilience.

Friendship’s Integrated Climate Adaptation Solution (ICAS) reflects this approach. It recognises that socioeconomic, climate, health, and geographic challenges were interconnected, and brought them together through locally led, nature-based action. In 2025, Friendship also became the first Bangladeshi organisation to win the Earthshot Prize, in recognition of its climate work.

While receiving the award, Runa Khan stated, “I chose to break free from the constraints of aristocracy, convention and performative goodness. I chose purpose over privilege, guided by empathy, truth, and ethical integrity, faith and trust in God. Always conscious, trying that no action of mine should cause harm. I started Friendship with these convictions, not through a predetermined plan, ambition, available funding or an agenda, but in response to genuine human need, and their unbearable suffering which I saw. As Friendship gre w, it carried within it the values by which I tried to live my life: integrity, dignity, justice, quality, hope and faith. To receive recognition that an organisation serving 7.5 million people could grow from integrity of purpose, rather than ambition means more to me than any award. It honours the beliefs that have guided my life – and to be awarded for it? It is like a dream, and gives me such humility – it is beyond anything I can express.”

Edgar O Chua, Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation Chairperson, said, "Though the paths of Tommy Koh, Runa Khan, and Bo Kyi differed, each reminds us that the true course of a life is forged by what we choose to do with the truths we encounter," said Chua. "They did not set out intent on bending the arc of history. They simply looked upon a broken world, recognised a wrong, and decided that they could not look away. The three 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Awardees we honour today remind us that the meaning of our journey is found not in avoiding these moments, but in having the courage to not look away, when they do happen," he added. "As we leave here today, let us carry that sensitivity forward, trusting that our small, everyday choices to stand with others has the power to shape a more compassionate future”.

Bangladesh’s Runa Khan receives Ramon Magsaysay Award

Three laureates, a shared commitment to change

Runa Khan was one of three recipients of the 2026 Award. The other laureates were Tommy Koh of Singapore, recognised for his contributions to diplomacy and international cooperation, and Bo Kyi of Myanmar, honoured for supporting political prisoners and survivors of torture, and advancing accountability and human rights. Together, the laureates represented humanitarian innovation, international cooperation, and the defence of human dignity.

The three laureates joined a distinguished roster of past recipients, including Nobel Peace Prize laureates Dr Muhammad Yunus and Mother Teresa, development leader Sir Fazle Hasan Abed, filmmaker Akira Kurosawa, and the Dalai Lama. The award acknowledged not only Khan’s leadership, but also the determination of the communities, colleagues, and supporters who had helped shape Friendship’s work.

item.title: 5 strategies that enable India to achieve remarkable success in reducing poverty
item.description:
In their poverty and equity brief published in October 2026, the World Bank reported that from 2011 to 2023, the percentage of people living in extreme poverty in India has significantly decreased from 27.1 per cent to 2.6 per cent. This remarkable achievement in poverty reduction has been recognised as one of the fastest in the world. Consequently, India has succeeded in lifting approximately 496 million people—more than the combined population of the United States and Russia—out of the poverty trap.

The World Bank report further stated that even when considering the poverty line set for lower-middle-income countries at $4.20 per day, the poverty rate in India has decreased from 57.7 per cent to 16.1 per cent during this time. However, the report cautions that part of this recent success in poverty reduction might also be due to improvements in measurement methods alongside genuine improvements in living standards.

Indeed, both financial and non-financial poverty indicators improved in India between 2011 and 2023. However, this improvement has not been uniform across all regions of the country; rather, 57 per cent of India’s total poor population is concentrated in a contiguous geographic area stretching from Uttar Pradesh to West Bengal.

The World Bank anticipates that poverty in India will continue to decrease in the future, although the pace of reduction is expected to be relatively slow. According to the World Bank's forecast, based on the $4.20 per day poverty line, India's poverty rate could decline from 14.2 per cent in 2026 to 12.1 per cent by 2028.

Beyond these statistics and trends, two fundamental questions arise. First, what factors have contributed to India’s significant success in poverty reduction? Second, what lessons can be learned from this experience? It can be presumed that four key reasons primarily drove the rapid reduction in India’s poverty rate.

The first reason is the maintenance of high economic growth over a long period. From 2010 to 2025, India consistently achieved high and stable economic growth, making it one of the world’s fastest-growing major economies. India’s economic growth began at 8.5 per cent in 2010. Despite a slight slowdown due to global and domestic financial contractions in the following four years, growth soon rebounded. In 2015-2016, the country’s real GDP growth was close to 8.3 per cent. Although the growth contracted during the COVID-19 pandemic, India achieved a historic growth rate of nearly 10 per cent in 2021. From 2022 to 2025, India averaged over 7 per cent economic growth. Such high growth over a long period has had a significantly positive impact on India’s poverty situation.

Firstly, India’s experience highlights the importance of reforms for long-term economic growth. Especially significant are reforms in the revenue and regulatory framework, structural changes in the economy to increase the GDP and employment share of the production sector, massive investments in infrastructure (including roads, highways, railways, IT connectivity), and the expansion of service-based sectors like IT, business services, and global capability centres, as well as the overall technological transformation of the economy.

The second reason for the success in poverty reduction in India is robust growth in consumption expenditure. Between 2015 and 2025, India experienced profound and consistent structural changes in personal consumption expenditure. During this period, the nation’s total family consumption expenditure nearly doubled, increasing from $1.24 trillion in 2015 to $2.24 trillion in 2025. Approximately 60 to 70 per cent of India’s total GDP comes from personal consumption expenditure. Hence, this decade-long surge in consumption expenditure has been one of the main driving forces behind the country’s high economic growth and poverty reduction.

Indian consumers’ inclination towards higher quality products has also become evident. That is, buyers have become more interested in purchasing high-quality goods instead of relatively cheaper products. Consequently, in the Indian household budget, the share of spending on non-essential goods and services has historically increased from 15 per cent to 36 per cent by 2025.

Simultaneously, Indian households have begun prioritising services and life experiences over tangible goods. For example, participating in cultural events, watching sports, attending music concerts, dining out, and engaging in recreational travel have become more prominent. Between 2020 and 2025, Indians’ spending on foreign travel increased from 270 million rupees to 400 million rupees.

The remarkable reduction in poverty in India over the past decade owes significantly to the increase in employment, especially for women. Between 2014 and 2024, India created over 170 million job opportunities, averaging 17 million new jobs annually. The unemployment rate in India decreased from 7.6 per cent in 2015 to 4.2 per cent in 2025. There have also been sectoral changes in employment structure. Although 41 per cent of India’s total labour force is still engaged in agriculture, the relative importance of agriculture in employment is gradually decreasing.

Currently, about 26 per cent of India’s total labour force is employed in the manufacturing and construction sectors, and the remaining 33 per cent in the service sector. Significant structural changes have also occurred in women’s labour force participation. While the employment-related ratio for women was around 22 per cent in the mid-2010s, it increased to over 40 per cent by 2025. The growth in wage-based and self-employment opportunities in rural and urban areas has played a major role in this regard.

The fourth reason for India’s significant poverty reduction is the unprecedented and silent revolution in the country’s social security system. Between 2015 and 2025, India expanded its social security programmes to cover 64 per cent of the total population, up from 19 per cent. This expansion has brought over 940 million citizens under at least one social security benefit. This initiative is one of the largest expansions of social safety nets in world history.

In 2019, only four states in India had regular monthly cash assistance programmes. By 2025, 17 out of India’s 28 states and Delhi had implemented monthly cash assistance programmes. These initiatives have significantly contributed to bringing the extreme poverty rate down to 2.6 per cent by 2023.

Additionally, providing financial assistance ranging from 1,000 to 2, 500 rupees per month to low-income families has offered vital support for their livelihoods. This has led to increased family savings, enhanced women's roles in managing family expenditures, and improved their societal status.
Now, let us consider what lessons can be learned from India’s recent historical experience in poverty reduction.

Firstly, India’s experience highlights the importance of reforms for long-term economic growth. Especially significant are reforms in the revenue and regulatory framework, structural changes in the economy to increase the GDP and employment share of the production sector, massive investments in infrastructure (including roads, highways, railways, IT connectivity), and the expansion of service-based sectors like IT, business services, and global capability centres, as well as the overall technological transformation of the economy.

Secondly, India’s growth strategy aimed not only at achieving long-term economic growth but also at making that growth pro-poor by increasing productive employment opportunities. In light of this experience, adopting an employment-driven growth strategy rather than a growth-driven employment strategy could be more effective for developing countries. This is because many countries have experienced jobless growth in the past. India has demonstrated that achieving high economic growth and high employment targets simultaneously is possible.

Other countries can learn from India's largest social security programmes, particularly regarding beneficiary verification, targeted benefits provision, programme implementation, evaluation, and necessary programme modifications.

Thirdly, India’s experience with consumption expenditure growth suggests focusing on increasing consumption growth in the rural economy rather than urban areas, which can enhance overall economic consumption. This is particularly relevant for countries where the majority of people live in rural areas. In India, significant shifts towards non-agricultural employment (currently making up 50 per cent of rural income) have caused real rural income growth to surpass urban wage growth rates.

This has been one of the main driving forces behind rapid consumption expenditure growth in India. The core lesson from this experience is to emphasise the rural economy and aid its rapid development to boost consumption in the economy. As economic growth increases, consumers will decrease the portion allocated to basic food expenses from their total expenditure and redirect that money towards products and services like electronics, mobile phones, automobiles, and luxury personal care items.

Fourthly, India’s experience in creating productive employment suggests that increasing human capacity, equitable distribution of resources, access to basic social services, and fairness in income distribution are essential. Similarly, ownership of assets at the family level also has a clear impact on future economic success. Creating more opportunities for girls and women and ensuring investments in their economic, legal, and political empowerment are crucial for employment growth.

Constitutional and legal reforms can directly increase women's participation in economic activities. Providing families with infrastructure facilities like alternative energy, water, and electricity enables women to engage in self-employment or participate in the labour market. Ensuring women's access to productive assets like land and loans is also essential for economic empowerment.

Fifthly, India’s experience in social security indicates the need to enhance adequate revenue allocation for such programmes and ensure their expansion across various geographic regions of the country. India’s social assistance programmes have also demonstrated how technological infrastructure or ‘tech stack’—like IT connectivity mechanisms—can expand the scope and effectiveness of programmes. In this context, women-centric welfare programmes, assistance in agriculture and rural sectors, and the expansion of the social assistance coverage are particularly important.

Other countries can learn from India's largest social security programmes, particularly regarding beneficiary verification, targeted benefits provision, programme implementation, evaluation, and necessary programme modifications.

Celebrating the significant success of poverty reduction in India should not merely focus on its achievements. More importantly, it is about learning from this experience and finding ways to apply those lessons to the poverty reduction efforts of other developing countries based on their specific realities and needs.

#Selim Jahan is the former Director of the Human Development Report Office of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).

item.title: Bangladesh recover from early blows as Tanzid hits fifty before lunch
item.description:
CRICKET-RSA-BAN-TEST

Bangladesh recovered from a disastrous start to reach 91-3 at lunch on the opening day of the first Test against South Africa, with opener Tanzid Hasan scoring an unbeaten half-century.

Bangladesh lost three wickets for just 22 runs after electing to bat in Johannesburg, but Tanzid and Towhid Hridoy steadied the innings with a 69-run partnership for the fourth wicket.

Tanzid remained unbeaten on 51, while Hridoy was batting on 23 at the interval.

Bangladesh opt to bat after winning toss against South Africa

Tanzid, who also scored a century against Australia in Darwin, registered his second Test fifty. He had struggled for runs in his previous five innings but found his form with some impressive strokes, despite surviving a couple of close calls.

South Africa pacer Kagiso Rabada dealt Bangladesh an early triple blow, taking all three wickets to fall.

On his Test debut, opener Mahfizul Islam was dismissed off the very first ball of the match, caught by Marco Jansen at gully. Mominul Haque followed shortly afterwards, caught behind off Rabada for seven.

Captain Najmul Hossain was the third to depart, bowled by Rabada for four after failing to negotiate a full-length delivery that swung back into him.

Bangladesh were reduced to 22-3 in nine overs before Tanzid and Hridoy began the recovery.
