item.title: IUBAT observes World Sustainability Day 2026
item.description:
The International University of Business Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT) observed World Sustainability Day 2026 on Wednesday, November 11, with discussions highlighting environmental protection, energy conservation, responsible water use, and quality education.
Organized by the university’s Department of Environmental Science on its campus, the program brought together university officials, faculty members, distinguished guests, and students to discuss contemporary sustainability challenges and possible solutions.
Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Abdur Rab chaired the program, emphasizing the importance of conserving energy and managing water resources responsibly. He called for collective efforts to promote sustainable practices in everyday life and institutional activities.
The event also featured an academic session where Department of Environmental Science faculty members Dr Md Shafiqul Islam, Dr M Rehan Dastagir, Dr Ferdous Ahmed, and Dr Mariyum Sultana Marry delivered presentations on various aspects of sustainability and environmental concerns.
Chief Guest Professor Dr Mahmudul Islam, founder of the Center for Disaster Management Education, Research and Training (DMERT), highlighted the role of inclusive and quality education in achieving sustainable development.
Focusing on Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4), he said quality education is essential to raising awareness, developing relevant knowledge and skills, and preparing future generations to address global challenges.
Special Guest Alamgir Hossain also spoke about the need for greater public awareness, environmental responsibility and active participation in addressing sustainability challenges.
The programme began with the national anthem, followed by a one-minute silence in memory of IUBAT Founder and former Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr M Alimullah Miyan and Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Mahmuda Khanom, acknowledging their contributions to the university.
Professor Dr Md Ataur Rahman, Chairman of the Department of Environmental Science, delivered the welcome address, highlighting the importance of environmental awareness and collective action.
The program concluded with a vote of thanks from Dr Nupur Momtaz, who acknowledged the contributions of the guests, university authorities, faculty members, organizers and students.
Through the observance, IUBAT reaffirmed its commitment to environmental education, responsible resource management, and academic initiatives promoting sustainability.

item.title: Bangladesh, Sri Lanka discuss expediting trade, investment negotiations
item.description:
Bangladesh and Sri Lanka on Sunday discussed expediting ongoing negotiations to promote bilateral trade and investment as part of efforts to strengthen cooperation between the two countries.
The discussion took place when Sri Lankan High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dharmapala Weerakkody paid a courtesy call on State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Dhaka, said a ministry press release.
During the meeting, they reviewed ongoing bilateral cooperation, including initiatives to expand trade and investment through faster progress in negotiations.
Kobir said Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, under their new leaderships, were pursuing nation-building in a pragmatic and forward-looking manner.
He underscored the mutual interest in exploring all possible avenues of cooperation to fulfill the aspirations of the peoples of both countries.
The state minister also recalled his interactions with Sri Lankan leaders on the sidelines of multilateral events.
He stressed the need to implement the decisions of the fourth Bangladesh-Sri Lanka Foreign Office Consultation held in Colombo in November 2025. The next consultation will take place in Dhaka.
Both sides expressed optimism about further deepening the longstanding and multifaceted relations between the two countries.

item.title: Milon urges ADB to boost support for education sector
item.description:
Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon has urged the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to step up its support for improving education standards and modernising the country's education system.
He made the call on Sunday when an ADB delegation, led by Gi Sun Song, director of the bank's Human and Social Development Division, paid a courtesy call on him at his office at the Secretariat.
The minister said the ADB had long played a significant role in Bangladesh's development and stressed the need for greater assistance to improve the quality of education and make the education system more responsive to contemporary needs.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was giving top priority to education, adding that the ADB could provide practical support in implementing the government's plans for the sector.
During the meeting, Gi Sun Song praised the initiatives taken to develop Bangladesh's education sector under the prime minister's leadership.
He said several ADB-funded programmes were already underway in Bangladesh, while a number of other projects were in the pipeline. The bank is keen to contribute further to the development of the country's education sector through these initiatives.
ADB Deputy Country Director Akira Matsunaga, Head of Country Operations Chandan Sapkota, Additional Secretary to the Ministry of Education Dr Sardar Md Keramat Ali, and other officials concerned were also present.

item.title: PM advises students to maintain cleanliness, show kindness to animals
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has advised students to maintain cleanliness, plant trees and treat all animals, including birds, with kindness and compassion.
He gave the advice during an interaction with students from several educational institutions at the National Parliament on Sunday.
During a recess in the parliamentary session, the students paid a courtesy call on the prime minister.
The delegation included 41 students who secured GPA-5 in the 2026 HSC examinations from various educational institutions in Patgram and Hatibandha upazilas of Lalmonirhat, along with six teachers and guardians.
Also present were 27 students from grades 10 and 11 and six teachers from The Aga Khan Academy, as well as 41 students and two teachers from the Department of Law at Brac University.
During the interaction, the prime minister expressed hope that the younger generation would take an interest in politics and state governance. However, he advised them to first develop themselves as qualified, skilled and responsible citizens before becoming involved in politics.
He offered three specific suggestions to the students.
First, he urged them to keep their cities, homes and surrounding areas clean and dispose of waste in designated places rather than littering.
Second, he encouraged them to plant at least one tree during the monsoon season to mark their own birthdays or those of family members.
Third, he called on them to show kindness and compassion towards all animals, including birds.
Earlier, the students attended a briefing at the National Parliament. They also visited the parliamentary library and observed a session of parliament. Later, they took part in a photo session at the North Plaza of the parliament building.
Information Minister Andalib Rahman, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister's Press Secretary Saleh Shibli, Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Ruman and Prime Minister's Private Secretary-2 Mehedul Islam were also present.

item.title: Dengue: 8 more die, 1,952 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Eight people died of dengue and 1,952 new patients were hospitalised across the country in the 24 hours to Sunday morning.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 499 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the new deaths, five were recorded in Dhaka division, while one each in Mymensingh, Chittagong and Khulna divisions.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 162,509 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 156,194 have recovered.
Currently, 5816 patients are receiving treatment at different hospitals across the country.

item.title: Moriyasu backs Japan to become world's best after Brazil triumph
item.description:
Coach Hajime Moriyasu said Japan can become the best in the world after beating Brazil for a second time, as he prepares to step down after eight years in charge.
Japan shocked the five-times world champions 3-2 in a friendly in Singapore on Saturday, with substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scoring an injury-time winner.
The victory came just more than a year after Japan beat Brazil for the first time in a friendly in Tokyo.
Brazil eliminated Japan from this year's World Cup in North America with a 2-1 win in the last 32.
Moriyasu will leave his job after a friendly against Paraguay on Tuesday but he is certain that Japan are on track to become a major football nation.
"The players showed confidence and courage and dug in when they needed to dig in," he said.
"At the World Cup in the future, Japan can absolutely become the world's best."
Moriyasu, Japan's longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa.
But the Asian Football Confederation announced that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to "exceptional circumstances" in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country.
The JFA confirmed on Friday that next week's game would be Moriyasu's last.
"Aiming for wins and growth, I will strive to do my best as I always have," Moriyasu said.
Japan were looking for revenge after a heart-breaking loss to Brazil at the World Cup.
Gabriel Martinelli scored in the 95th minute in Houston to send Brazil through.
Japan midfielder Ao Tanaka, who was in floods of tears after making a late mistake in the World Cup game, said after the win in Singapore that he was "calm but really happy".
"All sorts of things started coming back to me as the game got closer, and of course those frustrating memories were in my head," said the Leeds United midfielder.
Japan took an early 2-0 lead before Brazil hit back through two Vinicius Junior wonder strikes.
Coventry winger Sakamoto won it for Japan in injury time, before Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were sent off for protesting the goal.
The 30-year-old Sakamoto was making his first Japan appearance for five years.
"To come back like this and make a contribution in such a massive match, one we all really wanted to win, gives me so much confidence," said Sakamoto.

item.title: ‘We couldn’t do things we wanted,’ admits Dooley after SAFF heartbreak
item.description:
Bangladesh head coach Thomas Dooley admitted his side failed to execute their game plan as a late goal condemned the hosts to a heartbreaking 1-0 defeat against Pakistan in the SAFF Championship 2026 semi-final at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Saturday.
A 86th-minute strike from Denmark-based winger Abdul Samad Shahzad broke the hearts of nearly 20,000 home supporters, sending Pakistan into their first-ever SAFF final and ending Bangladesh's hopes of reaching the title decider for the first time since 2005.
Dooley felt Bangladesh struggled to cope with the pressure of playing a high-stakes knockout match in front of their home crowd, with his players unable to reproduce the fluent football they had displayed in their 4-0 victory over Sri Lanka in their final group fixture.
“Sometimes when you have that kind of pressure here, that you want to win on home ground and reach the final, some people react differently in that moment. Maybe that's a learning experience for young players on how to deal with a situation like that. It's a shock situation for the players, and some react differently,” Dooley said at the post-match press conference.
The German-American coach admitted he never felt Bangladesh had established superiority over their opponents throughout the contest, pointing to slow build-up play and a lack of composure in possession.
“Honestly, I never really had the feeling that we were much better than they were, not from the beginning, and not until the end. Sometimes when you play under pressure, you slow down a little bit, you think slower. I don't know, that's what I think,” he said.
Dooley revealed that he had urged his players at half-time to move the ball quicker from the back, but Bangladesh continued to struggle against Pakistan's anticipation and pressing.
Despite the disappointment, Dooley insisted Bangladesh were making progress, highlighting the team's development since his first match in charge against San Marino.
“Overall, it's a development process for the team, and I'm looking forward to developing even more, bringing new players in to learn the things we need. I am pleased with the big development from the first game we played in San Marino to the way we played last week,” he said.
He also suggested the outcome could have been different had Bangladesh maintained better passing accuracy and avoided the costly mistake that led to the winner.
“If our passing had been a little bit better, like we did in the second half, where we dominated a little bit more and played in their half until they played the long ball again and we made a mistake at the back, giving them the upper hand, things could have been different,” he added.
Bangladesh captain Hamza Choudhury, meanwhile, urged supporters not to single out goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon for blame after his misplaced throw-out led to Pakistan's decisive goal.
“Very, very, very heartbreaking. It is a huge heartbreak, not just for us, obviously for the fans and the nation. But it is the mercy of Allah, what else can I say,” Hamza told reporters.
“People cannot blame any of us. We all played 11 versus 11, so no one can blame any individual,” the midfielder added.
Dooley also defended his young goalkeeper, emphasising that mistakes are part of football, particularly under the pressure of a home semi-final.
“He's also a young player, and he also makes some mistakes. Like I always say, they are no robots. They have a brain and they have also pressure – home game, have to win,” the coach said.
The defeat leaves Bangladesh facing another wait for a SAFF final appearance, having last reached the title decider in 2005. Their ambition of reclaiming the regional crown, which they last won in 2003, also remains unfulfilled.

item.title: Shanto backs pace attack to make impact
item.description:
Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto oozed with confidence about his pacers' ability to make an impact despite knowing the stern challenge in playing in South African conditions.
Expressing his full confidence in his fast bowlers, he said he believes they can exploit the conditions for their desired result in the opening Test of the two-match series, starting on Sunday at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg.
"This (pace bowling) is the biggest change in Bangladesh cricket, especially in this format. We have got some quality fast bowlers, particularly for this kind of condition," Shanto said today at a press conference ahead of the first Test.
"Hasan, Taskin and everyone have been doing a great job for us. I believe they can do something special for the team here. Their skills and the preparation they have been doing over the last few years are outstanding."
Bangladesh have had limited time to prepare for the series following their recent Test assignment against West Indies. However, Shanto said the players were ready to adapt to the conditions, with some experienced members expected to guide the younger players.
"We don't have that much time to prepare according to the conditions. But as professional cricketers, we need to adjust. A few of the boys have experience playing here, and I think they can share that experience with the younger guys," he stated.
Bangladesh are yet to finalise their playing XI, with the team management considering whether to include an extra spinner or an additional batter.
Shanto indicated that three fast bowlers would feature in the combination, while the inclusion of a spinner was also likely. The lone spinner might be Mehidy Hasan Miraz, instead of Taijul Islam as per Shanto's indication.
"I think three pacers will definitely be there. A spinner should also be there because our spinners have been contributing well, particularly Mehidy Hasan Miraz in Australia. We may go with this combination, but we will have another look at the wicket tomorrow before making the final decision," the skipper opined.
Mominul Haque and Towhid Hridoy also would play as occasional spinners if needed alongside the specialist as it was evidenced those two bowlers bowling in the net ahead of the Test.
Shanto himself also highlighted the importance of allround contributions, revealing that Bangladesh have encouraged their specialist batters to bowl more regularly in practice.
He said Mominul Haque was encouraged to bowl regularly in the nets over the last few years, while Towhid Hridoy's bowling could also provide the team with an additional option.
Shanto stressed that Bangladesh's batting unit must deliver a strong first-innings total to put pressure on South Africa.
"It's important for the entire batting unit to perform in these conditions. Particularly, those who get set need to play long innings. Whether it is Tanzid Tamim or someone else, it is important," he said.
"Batting will certainly be challenging here. If we can put up a big total in the first innings, our bowling attack can compete very well."
Bangladesh head into the series after an encouraging nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, although their subsequent Test results have not been particularly impressive.
Shanto said the team had discussed its recent shortcomings but was determined to focus on the challenges ahead rather than dwell on previous defeats.
"Mentally, everyone is in a good position. It's true that our last two or three matches haven't gone well, but instead of worrying too much about that, it's important to focus on how we can do better," he said.
Bangladesh's previous ODI series victory in South Africa also offers some encouragement, according to Shanto, who believes that success provides evidence that the team can perform well in the country.

item.title: Bangladesh eye historic breakthrough against South Africa
item.description:
Bangladesh will seek to rewrite their disappointing Test record against South Africa when they take on the hosts in a two-match series, hoping their resurgent pace attack and improved overseas performances can help them overcome one of their toughest challenges.
The task, however, is daunting. South Africa have traditionally been a formidable force at home, where pace, bounce and movement make conditions difficult for visiting teams. Even Australia, unarguably the most successful sides in Test cricket, have recently experienced the challenges of playing in South African conditions.Bangladesh's record against the Proteas offers little encouragement.
In 16 previous Tests between the sides, Bangladesh have suffered 14 defeats, while the remaining two ended in draws due to bad weather. Nine of those defeats came by an innings, underlining the scale of the challenge facing the visitors.
Despite the gloomy statistics, Bangladesh are drawing confidence from their recent landmark success in Australia and the emergence of a more potent pace attack.
Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, Shoriful Islam and Ebadot Hossain have demonstrated their ability to trouble opposition batters in challenging overseas conditions. South African pitches, with their natural pace and bounce, could provide an ideal setting for the quartet to make an impact.
Chief selector Habibul Bashar Sumon admitted the difficulty of the assignment but remained hopeful of an upset.
"South Africa are particularly strong at home and the conditions will be difficult for us. We need to play exceptionally well to win," Bashar said.
He believes Bangladesh's improved pace attack could make a significant difference if the batters provide adequate support.
"Our pacers have been a great revolution of late as they produced remarkable performance in challenging overseas conditions. If our batters can complement them, I think we can overcome the South Africa Test," he added.
Bangladesh's confidence, however, suffered a setback following their 1-0 home Test series defeat against the West Indies. The series also raised questions about the team's decision to prepare spin-friendly pitches despite having developed a promising pace attack.
The South Africa tour now presents an opportunity for Bangladesh to put that disappointment behind them and demonstrate their growing ability to compete away from home.
The opening Test at the Wanderers is expected to be particularly challenging for Bangladesh's batters, with Johannesburg, the venue of the second Test traditionally offering assistance to fast bowlers through extra pace and bounce.
The visitors will also have to contend with a formidable South African pace attack featuring Kagiso Rabada, Marco Jansen, Anrich Nortje and Dane Paterson.
Bangladesh's top order will therefore be under considerable pressure to negotiate the new ball, withstand the opening-session examination and build substantial partnerships.
Bashar admitted that batting inconsistency remains a major concern but expressed confidence in the players' ability to respond.
"I admit our batting has been inconsistent. But at the same time, I believe they will come back strongly," he said.
The series also carries significant importance for Bangladesh's World Test Championship (WTC) campaign.
Bangladesh are currently fifth in the standings with 45.83 percentage points from three victories in eight Tests. South Africa, meanwhile, occupy second position with 71.43 percentage points after winning five of their seven matches.
The reigning WTC champions strengthened their position in the race for the final with a 2-1 home series victory over Australia. Under the WTC points system, teams receive 12 points for a victory, four for a draw and six for a tie, with final standings determined by the percentage of points earned.
Bangladesh have four Tests remaining in the current cycle, with two against South Africa and two against England at home. They can collect a maximum of 48 additional points from those matches, potentially lifting their points percentage to 63.89 if they win all four.
A competitive performance in South Africa would therefore be vital not only for breaking their long-standing winless record against the Proteas but also for keeping their hopes of qualifying for the 2027 WTC final alive.

item.title: Sabalenka sorry for outburst in Svitolina defeat
item.description:
Aryna Sabalenka apologized on Saturday after an on-court outburst during her defeat to Ukrainian rival Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
Footage shared widely on social media appeared to show the former world number one swearing in a tirade that some commenters interpreted as directed towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general.
However, Sabalenka said Saturday that she lost her cool due to the behavior of spectators during Friday's 3-6, 6-3, 1-6 defeat, which sent the four-time Grand Slam-winner crashing out.
"I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online," Sabalenka wrote in a post on Instagram.
"My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes and I reacted emotionally in the moment.
"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament."
Svitolina, who has refused to shake hands with tennis players from Russia and its regional ally Belarus since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, acknowledged that a match against Sabalenka could carry extra weight for her fans.
"As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags ... and of course they want me to win this particular match," she said Saturday when asked about Sabalenka's statement.
"We've played many times with Aryna ... she has her fans. I have my fans," added Svitolina, who reached the Finals title match with a win over Linda Noskova on Saturday.
"I have seen the glimpse of it because obviously it's in the social media," she said. "(I) just hope the matches between us (are) respected. Sometimes in some matches that we've played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war.
"It is like this in the social media sometimes the things are turned around a little bit."

item.title: Andreeva beats Pegula to book WTA Finals title clash with Svitolina
item.description:
French Open winner Mirra Andreeva beat Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 on Saturday to book a WTA Finals title showdown with former champion Elina Svitolina in Indian Wells, California.
Ukraine's Svitolina, who won the WTA Finals in 2018, fell to Ashleigh Barty in the final in the following year but hadn't been back since, powered past Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-1 to give herself a shot at another triumph in the elite season-ending event.
"It's really magical to be back in the finals," Svitolina said. "Just very special for me to have this opportunity (Sunday), to have another battle another challenge."
The 32-year-old, back in the top 10 this year for the first time since before her daughter, Skai, was born in 2022, will face a rising star in 19-year-old Andreeva.
The Russian teen won her maiden major at Roland Garros this year and with her victory over Pegula is assured of rising from third to second in the world rankings.
Andreeva remained unbeaten in her WTA Finals singles debut, having posted round robin victories over sixth-ranked Svitolina, world number two Aryna Sabalenka and Diana Shnaider.
She's the youngest player to make the final since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 and joined Serena Williams and Chris Evert as the only players to win their first four matches in the event in straight sets.
"I think I can be very proud of myself," she told Tennis Channel. "I'm very happy with how I'm playing. I'm very happy also with how I deal with the pressure. I knew this match had a lot on the line."
For Pegula it was a match of missed chances, the fifth-ranked American unable to build on early breaks in both sets.
Andreeva double-faulted on break point to give Pegula a 2-1 lead in the opening set.
But the Russian broke back immediately, whipping a crosscourt forehand winner on her third break chance to make it 2-2.
Andreeva saved a pair of break points in the fifth game and broke again for a 5-3 lead.
Pegula had a chance to extend the set in the next game, but on break point she smashed what looked to be an easy backhand at the net past the baseline and Andreeva held to pocket the first.
Andreeva double-faulted to give Pegula a break chance in the fourth game of the second and the American converted for an imposing 3-1 lead.
But once again Andreeva broke back immediately, winning five of the last six games to close out the victory in one hour and 25 minutes.
Svitolina said she did "pretty much everything" well against Noskova, who crumbled with 11 double faults as the Ukrainian surged to victory in just 65 minutes.
The Czech is second on the WTA Tour's aces list behind Elena Rybakina but had just two -- the second to save a match point in the penultimate game.
Noskova took the game, but it was a brief reprieve. In the next Svitolina took the match on her third match point when a Noskova forehand slid wide.
"I think I played really well today, serving good, returning well, too," Svitolina said. "I was able to play aggressive and find the angles."
The round robin format means Svitolina will have the chance, rare in tennis, of avenging her lopsided Monday loss to Andreeva in the same tournament.
"She's in good form, but I feel like I've found my game since I lost the first match against her," Svitolina said. "I will do my homework with my coaches and try to find the key."

item.title: Holding the NBR accountable
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue’s (NBR) latest push to develop a specialized app to collect a 0.2% advance tax -- deducting Tk2 per thousand on goods supplied via distributors starting next January is yet another display of the National Board of Revenue’s (NBR) reactive decision making.
While bringing informal businesses into the formal tax net and digitizing transactions are sound principles in theory, the timing and execution of this move expose a deeply flawed administrative mindset.
That NBR is already facing a staggering revenue shortfall exceeding Tk50,000 crore in just the first four months of FY27 brings to light all we need to know about the institution’s inability to set realistic targets.
Moreover, the tax authority is once again taking the path of least resistance: Potentially squeezing small, vulnerable shopkeepers because it lacks the competence and political will to collect from the wealthy elite.
For years, the NBR and the Ministry of Finance have indulged in the annual farce of setting wildly unrealistic, inflated revenue targets disconnected from ground realities. When those projections inevitably collapse, the agency panics and unleashes predatory compliance burdens on the smallest economic actors.
Instead of dismantling entrenched tax evasion among the powerful and wealthy, be they corporate conglomerates or individuals, they continue targeting individual middle class employees and the millions of small retail traders who are already battling sluggish sales and relentless inflation.
Expecting a corner shop owner to maintain five separate VAT registers, hire accountants, and absorb advance tax deductions is administrative harassment disguised as reform. Inevitably, these compounding compliance costs then get passed directly onto struggling consumers through higher retail prices.
It is unacceptable that taxpayers continue to pay the price for chronic regulatory incompetence without any repercussions for the officials responsible for perpetual revenue failures.
If we want true fiscal reform, then we must be setting realistic targets, automating collection from high-income tax evaders, and holding NBR leadership accountable for its systemic collection failures every year.

item.title: Paving the way for women to lead
item.description:
We agree with Speaker Major (retd) Hafiz Uddin Ahmed that giving women the opportunity to win 100 parliamentary seats through direct elections, rather than confining them to the existing reserved-seat system, is the way forward if we care about genuine political empowerment of women.
As this newspaper noted in our previous editorial, "Where are the women leaders?," Bangladesh's democratic landscape suffers from a staggering deficit of female decision-makers. That in the 2026 parliamentary election, women secured a dismal seven general seats is simply unacceptable, and that more is not being done to rectify this glaring issue is a failure of the state.
The message is unmistakable: While women stand at the vanguard of street movements and grassroots campaigns, patriarchal party structures systematically lock them out when power is distributed.
For far too long, the reserved-seat mechanism has been used by major political parties as a convenient smokescreen to avoid nominating women for general constituencies. This must end.
Appointed rather than elected, reserved-seat lawmakers frequently lack direct constituency authority and are treated as secondary actors in legislative chambers.
Moving toward 100 directly elected seats for women would shatter this patronizing status quo, legitimizing female leaders through popular mandates and giving them undeniable political weight.
Empowering half the population is not merely a matter of social justice but an absolute prerequisite for national development, especially at a time when regressive beliefs threaten to infiltrate our politics.
No nation, and certainly not ours, can hope to build a resilient, modern economy while sidelining the talent, perspective, and leadership of 50% of its citizens.
We need the government, and by extension the leaders of all political parties, to move swiftly from rhetorical endorsement to constitutional and electoral reform.
Dismantling tokenism and establishing direct electoral pathways for women is an obvious, non-negotiable step forward. It is time to stop treating female representation as political charity and let women claim their rightful place as equal architects of our future.

item.title: ULAB students organize marketplace to mark Sukumar Ray’s birth anniversary
item.description:
The School of Business at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) organized a student-run marketplace on November 14 to mark the 139th birth anniversary of Bengali litterateur Sukumar Ray.
Titled “The Abol Tabol Marketplace,” the event was held at the Game Area of ULAB’s permanent campus as part of an initiative called “Project Nonsense,” organized by Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) students.
The initiative aimed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and practical business experience by allowing students to apply their knowledge of marketing, finance, operations and entrepreneurship in a real marketplace.
Eminent theatre personality and essayist Alok Basu attended the event as the chief guest, while ULAB Vice-Chancellor Professor Shamsad Mortuza was present as the special guest.
A F Wazir Ahmad, head of the Department of Business Administration and associate professor, also attended, along with faculty members from different departments.
Students set up and operated stalls showcasing business ideas and creative products. They gained practical experience in developing business plans, promoting products, managing finances and interacting directly with customers.
Inspired by the imagination, satire and creativity in Sukumar Ray’s literary works, the marketplace provided students with an opportunity to explore business concepts outside the traditional classroom setting.
A drawing competition for children was also held as part of the celebration, with renowned artist Chitra Sultana in attendance. The participation of children added a creative element to the event.
The initiative sought to promote practical business skills, experiential learning and creative thinking among students through entrepreneurial activities and creative engagements.

item.title: What makes beetroot worth adding to your daily diet?
item.description:
Beetroot is a nutrient-rich vegetable that can be enjoyed in several ways, including in salads, juices, smoothies, and cooked dishes. It contains natural nitrates, folate, potassium, vitamin C, and various antioxidants that support several bodily functions. Its potential benefits are particularly associated with blood pressure regulation, improved blood circulation, and physical exercise performance.
However, no single food can guarantee good health. Including beetroot as part of a balanced and varied diet is more important than relying on it for specific health benefits. Nutritionist Nami Agarwal has also highlighted several potential benefits of adding beetroot to regular meals.
Beetroot contains natural nitrates that help the body produce nitric oxide, a compound that allows blood vessels to relax and widen. This can improve blood flow and support healthy circulation. As a result, consuming beetroot may help regulate blood pressure and support cardiovascular health.
People who regularly walk, run, or exercise may benefit from including beetroot in their diet. Its natural nitrate content can support blood circulation and oxygen delivery to the muscles. This may help improve physical performance and endurance, particularly during exercise.
Beetroot contains antioxidants and plant compounds that help the body combat oxidative stress. These compounds may also support normal liver function by protecting cells against oxidative damage. However, beetroot should not be considered a treatment for liver disease, and people with liver conditions should follow appropriate medical advice.
Beetroot contains several phytonutrients and antioxidants, some of which have anti-inflammatory properties. Including it in a balanced diet may help support the body's natural defense against oxidative stress and contribute to overall health.
Beetroot is a good source of folate, potassium, and vitamin C, all of which play important roles in maintaining normal bodily functions. Folate supports cell growth and division, while potassium helps regulate various bodily processes. Vitamin C contributes to immune function and other essential processes. Adding beetroot alongside other vegetables can therefore help improve dietary variety.
Beetroot can be eaten raw in salads, boiled, added to cooked dishes, or blended into juices and smoothies. However, eating the whole vegetable is generally preferable to relying solely on beetroot juice, as the whole vegetable also provides dietary fiber. Combining it with other colorful fruits and vegetables can further increase the nutritional variety of meals.
Although beetroot is nutritious, individual dietary needs and health conditions vary. People with specific health concerns or those taking regular medication should consult a doctor or nutritionist before making large amounts of beetroot a regular part of their diet.

item.title: Winter skincare: Four essential steps to keep your skin healthy
item.description:
Keeping your skin healthy and fresh does not require an extensive collection of skincare products. Whether it is winter or summer, following four basic steps, commonly known as the CTML routine, may be enough to maintain healthy skin throughout the year.
As winter approaches, dry and tight skin becomes a familiar concern. Many people turn to serums, ampoules, petroleum jelly, heavy moisturizers, olive oil, and almond oil to protect their skin from dryness.
However, instead of layering multiple products, a growing skincare approach known as 'skinimalism' encourages people to simplify their routines. The idea is to meet the skin's basic needs with fewer products rather than overwhelming it with unnecessary ingredients.
But is a minimal skincare routine enough to protect the skin during the colder months?
According to Sharmin Kochi, chief beauty expert at Bindia Exclusive Beauty Care, skinimalism is not merely a passing trend but a universal and healthy approach to skincare.
With social media promotions encouraging increasingly complicated eight-to-10-step routines, many people have become accustomed to using numerous skincare products. However, maintaining healthy and fresh skin does not necessarily require so many steps.
Whether in winter or summer, following four basic steps, known as CTML, can help maintain skin health throughout the year.
The four steps of the CTML routine are:
Keeping the skin clean is the first step towards maintaining its health. During winter, dirt, dust, and dead skin cells can accumulate on the skin. At this time, oil-based cleansers may be a better option than foaming cleansers.
Double cleansing can also be considered. The process involves first massaging the face with an oil-based cleanser to loosen dirt and impurities, followed by washing with a gel-based or water-based face wash.
Rather than applying moisturizer immediately after washing the face, using a toner can be part of the routine. According to Kochi, a toner helps maintain the skin's pH balance and keeps it soft and refreshed. She recommends water-based toners as a suitable option for Bangladesh's climate.
After toning, applying a moisturizer suited to one's skin type helps retain moisture and prevent dryness. Choosing the right formulation is particularly important during winter, when the skin tends to lose moisture more quickly.
The thin skin on the lips is also exposed to cold and dry weather, making it prone to moisture loss and cracking. Regularly applying lip balm or lip gel helps keep the lips moisturized and prevents them from becoming excessively dry.
Even with a minimal skincare routine, selecting products according to individual skin types remains important, Kochi said.
Oily and sensitive skin: Heavy or oil-based creams may clog pores and aggravate acne in people with oily skin. Lightweight, water-based gel moisturizers are generally a better choice. Those with acne or melasma should also use sunscreen regularly. Oil-free or powder-based sunscreen formulations may be suitable options.
Dry skin: Dry skin loses moisture more quickly during winter and therefore requires additional care. Cream-based or oil-based moisturizers containing nourishing ingredients can help protect the skin and maintain hydration.
Combination skin: People with combination skin should avoid excessively heavy skincare products. Lightweight, water-based moisturizers can help maintain a balance between oil and moisture, keeping the skin comfortable and refreshed.
Many people forget to apply sunscreen during winter, assuming that the mild sunlight poses little risk to their skin. However, Kochi emphasizes that sunscreen is not a seasonal skincare product.
Even when the sun does not feel particularly strong, exposure to sunlight can still affect the skin.
She also notes that prolonged exposure to heat from kitchen stoves may contribute to pigmentation and dark spots. Therefore, using sunscreen with SPF 30+ to 50+ during winter is important, depending on sun exposure and individual needs.
Rather than waiting until winter is in full swing to change skincare habits, starting early can help protect the skin from seasonal dryness, Kochi said.
Maintaining a consistent routine of cleansing, toning, and moisturizing before the weather becomes particularly dry can help preserve the skin's moisture. This may reduce the chances of the skin becoming rough, flaky, or uncomfortable during colder days.
Instead of overwhelming the skin with unnecessary products, a simple and consistent routine using a few suitable essentials can help keep it healthy, soft and fresh throughout winter.

item.title: High Court issues directives to control noise pollution
item.description:
The High Court Division has issued interim directives to control noise pollution, including regulating the use of fireworks and unnecessary vehicle horns and conducting regular drives in designated silent zones.
A Division Bench comprising Justice Sikder Mahmudur Razi and Justice Fatema Anwar issued the directives following a preliminary hearing of a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA), registered as case No 14939/2026.
The court also issued a rule asking the authorities concerned to explain why their failure to control noise pollution under existing laws and policies should not be declared illegal, contrary to public interest and public safety, and a violation of citizens' constitutional right to life under Articles 31 and 32.
The rule also seeks an explanation on why directions should not be issued to formulate and implement a coordinated, time-bound action plan to control noise pollution in silent zones and pollution caused by construction work, industrial establishments, social events, festivals and vehicles.
The court issued the following interim directives to the Inspector General of Police, director general of the Department of Environment, chairmen of the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) and Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK), commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), and administrators of Dhaka North and Dhaka South City Corporations:
The court directed the authorities concerned to submit reports on compliance with the directives every 3 months.
The respondents in the case include the secretaries of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Road Transport and Highways Division under the Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges; the Inspector General of Police; the DMP commissioner; the director general of the Department of Environment; the chairmen of BRTA and RAJUK; and the administrators of Dhaka North and Dhaka South City Corporations.
Dhaka, home to more than 2.2 crore people, frequently ranks among the world's most noise-polluted cities. Major sources of noise include unnecessary honking and hydraulic horns, industrial activities, construction work, generators, loud music at social events, uncontrolled use of microphones and loudspeakers, and fireworks.
Under the Noise Pollution (Control) Rules, 2025, areas within 100 meters of hospitals, educational institutions, offices and courts are designated as silent zones. The rules also regulate the use of fireworks and firecrackers and empower police to control prohibited vehicle horns.
In Dhaka, designated silent zones include a 3km radius around Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, the Secretariat and surrounding areas, Agargaon, the Parliament Building, the Prime Minister's Office area, Dhaka North City Corporation, Gulshan, Banani, Baridhara and Niketan.
BELA filed the case citing continued violations of prescribed noise levels in these areas and a lack of effective monitoring by the relevant authorities.
Md Ashraf Ali, Barrister-at-Law, represented BELA in the case, assisted by Advocate Hasanul Banna.

item.title: Hridoy leads Bangladesh’s fightback with record stand against South Africa
item.description:
CRICKET-RSA-BAN-TEST

Towhid Hridoy produced a remarkable innings of 137 to rescue Bangladesh from a disastrous start and guide them to 327 for 6 on the opening day of the first Test against South Africa in Johannesburg on Sunday.

Hridoy and Litton Das put together a fightback that became a record-breaking 206-run sixth-wicket partnership, the highest stand by Bangladesh against South Africa in Test cricket. Their effort transformed the visitors’ position after they had lost three wickets for just 22 runs.

Hridoy was eventually dismissed by Marco Jansen off the final ball of the day, ending an innings that had given Bangladesh a strong platform. Litton remained unbeaten on 92 at stumps, with Bangladesh finishing on 327 for 6, their highest ever team total in a Test against South Africa.

The day had begun in the worst possible fashion for Bangladesh. Making his Test debut, opener Mahfijul Islam was caught at gully by Jansen off Kagiso Rabada from the very first ball of the innings. Mominul Haque followed soon after, caught behind off Rabada for seven, leaving Bangladesh reeling at 7 for 2.

Rabada struck again to remove captain Najmul Hossain, who was bowled for 9, reducing Bangladesh to 22 for 3 inside nine overs. The South African fast bowler would go on to claim all five of Bangladesh’s first five wickets, registering his 18th five-wicket haul in Test cricket. He also became the first bowler to take five fifers against Bangladesh in Tests.

With the top order dismantled, Hridoy joined Tanzid Hasan at the crease. The pair resisted South Africa’s attack and gradually rebuilt the innings, putting on 99 runs for the fourth wicket.

It was Bangladesh’s highest partnership on South African soil, surpassing the previous record of 84 between Habibul Bashar and Hannan Sarkar at Potchefstroom in 2002.

Tanzid, who had struggled in his previous five Test innings, made a timely return to form. He scored 51, his second Test half-century, providing the resistance Bangladesh desperately needed. Hridoy, meanwhile, continued to bat with composure and determination, reaching his third consecutive fifty plus score in Test cricket.

The partnership ended when Rabada dismissed Tanzid, who dragged a short delivery onto his stumps. Mushfiqur Rahim fell to the next ball, caught at third slip, leaving Bangladesh at 108 for 5. Rabada had taken two wickets in the same over and completed his five-wicket haul.

At that point, the innings was in danger of falling apart. Instead, Hridoy and Litton launched a remarkable recovery.

The two batters combined patience with positive strokeplay, steadily taking the attack to the South African bowlers. Hridoy brought up his half-century and then his century, while Litton grew increasingly assured at the other end. Their partnership passed 100 to become the first century stand by Bangladesh in a Test in South Africa.

It also surpassed the 99-run fourth-wicket stand between Tanzid and Hridoy, which had broken the previous record for Bangladesh in South Africa only a few hours earlier.

The pair went on to set another milestone. Their 206-run partnership became Bangladesh’s highest against South Africa in Tests, eclipsing the previous record of 138 set by Zakir Ali and Mehidy Hasan Miraz in Mirpur in 2024.

Hridoy’s century was particularly significant given the circumstances in which he came to the crease. He had arrived with Bangladesh three wickets down for only 22 runs and had to rebuild the innings against a formidable South African pace attack.

The century was his second in Test cricket, following his unbeaten 242 in the previous Test against the West Indies in Sylhet. He had also scored 82 in the second innings of that match.

His dismissal on the final delivery of the day, trapped lbw by Jansen, brought an end to an innings of 137 and the record stand with Litton. But it did little to diminish the significance of his contribution.

Litton will resume on 92 not out on the second morning, with Bangladesh in a far stronger position than seemed possible during the opening exchanges.

Earlier in the day, after winning the toss, Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain had elected to bat, saying the team hoped to post a good total on a dry-looking surface. The visitors fielded three specialist fast bowlers and one spinner, with Mahfizul making his Test debut.

By the end of the day, Bangladesh had not only recovered from a collapse but also recorded their highest total against South Africa in Tests. Much of that turnaround owed to Hridoy’s outstanding 137 and his partnership with Litton, which gave the visitors a memorable first day in Johannesburg.

item.title: Tarique Rahman asks BNP, its 3 affiliated organisations to remain active on the streets
item.description:
The BNP has decided to remain active with political programmes in the field, not as a counteraction or precautionary measure against anyone, but with December, the month of victory, ahead.

Alongside the party, its affiliated organisations, the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, Jubo Dal, and Swechchhasebak Dal, will also carry out separate programmes throughout the month. Through this, the top leadership of the BNP aims to keep the party and its affiliated organisations active and invigorated organisationally.

This decision was made during a nearly two-hour meeting today, Sunday, at the Prime Minister's office in the National Assembly with the Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman, as well as the top leaders of the party and its three affiliated organisations.

The meeting was attended by BNP's Acting Secretary-General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi and the party's five Joint Secretary-Generals Shahid Uddin Chowdhury, Habib-Un-Nabi Khan Sohel, Khairul Kabir Khokon, Emran Saleh Prince, and Abdus Salam, along with leaders from the Chhatra Dal, Jubo Dal, Swechchhasebak Dal, and the conveners and member secretaries of the Dhaka Metropolitan North and South BNP.

This decision by the ruling BNP comes amidst various activities by leaders and activitists of the Awami League whose activities now banned and its allied organisations in different parts of the country following Sheikh Hasina's announcement of returning to the country in December after taking asylum in India due to the July mass uprising.

According to meeting sources, Tarique Rahman instructed the BNP and its affiliated organisations to formulate separate programmes to remain active in the field. However, these programmes will not be counter-actions against any party or faction. Similarly, no programmes will be adopted similar to how the Awami League in the past tried to thwart BNP programmes by setting up guards in neighborhoods.

The meeting sources revealed plans to implement protests, rallies, sit-in programmes, or cultural activities as political programmes. The BNP and its three affiliated organisations will independently announce these programmes.

Additionally, BNP-affiliated professional organisations have also been directed to remain active in the field by announcing separate programmes.

After a long period of opposition politics and movements and coming to power, the BNP now wants to increase organisational activities of the party and its allied organisations.

Especially centered around the month of victory, the party's leadership has planned to keep leaders and workers active in the field through ongoing political programmes.

When asked about this, BNP's Acting Secretary-General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi told Prothom Alo, "It's nothing special. We will have programmes similar to those we usually give during the month of victory in December."

item.title: ICBC 2026 to bring global scholars together to bridge cultures and disciplines
item.description:
Building on the success of its inaugural edition in 2024, the Multidisciplinary Biennial International Conference on Bridging Cultures: Advanced Discourses (ICBC 2026), Chapter II, will bring together an international community of scholars, researchers, academics and students from 20 to 26 November 2026.

Organised in a hybrid format, the conference will feature academic sessions hosted by City University on 20, 22 and 23 November, followed by a full-day, in-person programme at Bishwo Shahitto Kendro (BSK) in Dhaka on 26 November.

The four-day academic programme is expected to feature eight keynote speakers, 15 individual plenary speakers from Bangladesh and abroad, around 100 research paper presenters and approximately 300 participants. 

Building on the spirit of the 2024 edition, this year's conference will further expand its international reach and interdisciplinary engagement.

The inaugural address at the onsite programme will be delivered by Dr Mostofa Sarwar, Professor Emeritus of Geophysics at the University of New Orleans, USA, and the initiator of ICBC 2026. A distinguished scientist and academic, Professor Sarwar's intellectual interests also extend to literature and the humanities.

The opening online keynote address, scheduled for 20 November, will be delivered by Professor Dr Azfar Hussain, a Bangladeshi-American theorist, critic and interdisciplinary academic affiliated with the Global Center for Advanced Studies (GCAS) and Grand Valley State University, USA. Widely recognised for his engaging public lectures and interdisciplinary scholarship, Professor Hussain will set the intellectual tone for the conference.

The eight keynote speakers are Professor Dr Mostofa Sarwar, Professor Emeritus of Geophysics and former Associate Provost at the University of New Orleans, USA; Professor Dr Khaliquzzaman Elias of North South University and Jahangirnagar University; Professor Dr Azfar Hussain, Vice-President and Professor at GCAS and Professor of Interdisciplinary Studies at Grand Valley State University, USA; Professor Dr Renée AP Bricker of the University of North Georgia, USA; Professor Dr Beatrice de Salles of the University of San Francisco, USA; Professor Dr Johann Malawana, founder of the Healthcare Leadership Academy and Medics Academy, UK; Professor Dr Shamsad Mortuza, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) and Professor of English at the University of Dhaka; and Professor Mashrur Shahid Hossain of Jahangirnagar University, Bangladesh.

The 15 plenary speakers represent a wide range of disciplines and academic institutions. They include Professor Dr Maswood Akhter, Professor Dr Sarker Hasan Al Zayed, Ms Shahnaj Parvin, Ms Tina Nandi, Professor Dr Md Maniruzzaman, Professor Dr Laizu Nasrin, Ms Moumita Haque Shenjutee, Professor Dr Mohit Ul Alam, Professor Dr Shamim Reza, Professor Rokhsana Chowdhury, Professor Dr Md Masood Imran and Professor Dr Anirudha Kahaly, alongside other distinguished participants from Bangladesh and abroad. 

Their areas of expertise include comparative and postcolonial literature, translation, linguistics, cultural studies, gender studies, archaeology, heritage and Bangla literature.

The keynote and plenary sessions will bring together distinguished voices from universities and research institutions in Bangladesh and overseas. Discussions will cover comparative literature, cultural studies, the humanities and sciences, and the expanding role of artificial intelligence in academia and beyond.

Professor Dr Rahman M. Mahbub, Chair of the Conference, emphasises that a conference should be more than a gathering of scholars; it should be “a meeting of minds” — a shared space in which to question established assumptions and imagine more humane, inclusive and sustainable futures. 

He says ICBC seeks to build bridges across cultures and languages, literature and philosophy, the humanities and sciences, theory and practice, and technological innovation and human values.

Emphasising the urgency of this mission in the age of artificial intelligence, Professor Mahbub argues that technological progress must remain grounded in ethical judgement, empathy, imagination and human responsibility. 

As he puts it, “The humanities give knowledge a human soul, while science expands the possibilities of human action.” 

He maintains that these are not competing domains but inseparable partners in the progress of humankind.

ICBC 2026 is jointly organised by City University, the Department of English Language and Literature, IBC Foundation, and IDEAS: International Journal of Literature, Arts, Science & Culture.

item.title: Hridoy hits century against South Africa
item.description:
CRICKET-RSA-BAN-TEST

Towhid Hridoy continued his remarkable run with the bat, scoring another century as Bangladesh recovered from an early collapse to reach 289 for five in 77 overs against South Africa in Johannesburg on Sunday.

Hridoy reached the milestone with a four down to deep backward point in the 75.4 over off Dane Paterson.

Hridoy celebrated his double hundred in Sylhet slowly removing his helmet, placing it on the end of his bat and raising it aloft. The same celebration was seen in Johannesburg after his century against South Africa.

Having struck a double century in the Sylhet Test, Hridoy has now scored a hundred against South Africa, becoming only the second Bangladesh batter to achieve the feat.

Playing only his fourth Test, Hridoy walked in with Bangladesh in trouble at 22 for three. He then produced a remarkable innings, putting the team back on track with a crucial partnership alongside Litton Das.

The pair also set a new record, registering Bangladesh’s highest partnership against South Africa, home or away. The previous record was held by Jaker Ali and Mehidy Hasan Miraz, who added 138 runs in Mirpur in 2024.

The partnership remained unbeaten with 200 runs at the time of filing of this report. Hridoy is batting on 134 and Litton on 89.
